Title: Man drowns after falling into fish pond
Article:
GURUN: A man drowned after falling into a fish pond in front of a school in Kampung Batu 3, Jalan Jeniang, here, last night.
Kedah Fire and Rescue Department Zone 2 chief Senior Fire Superintendent II Mohd Naim Matt Jaaffar said they received an emergency call regarding the incident at 5.46pm yesterday.
He said a team of seven personnel from the Guar Chempedak Fire and Rescue Station, led by Senior Fire Officer II Zayati Muda, was dispatched to the scene.
"Information gathered from workers at the location indicated that the victim had fallen into the fish pond and was suspected to have drowned.
"Firefighters subsequently conducted a search and rescue operation using the surface-searching method before discovering the victim's body at 9.16pm," he said in a statement.
He added that the body was retrieved and handed over to the police for further action.
"No identification documents were found on the victim, who is estimated to be in his 30s.
"Health Ministry medical personnel present at the scene confirmed the victim's death," he said, adding that the operation ended at 11.19pm.
The operation was assisted by a team from the Sungai Petani Fire and Rescue Station, the Padang Lembu Volunteer Fire Brigade, police, and the Health Ministry.

Title: UNICEF estimates 20 million children suffered online sexual abuse in one year
Article:
GENEVA: About 20 million internet-using children across 21 countries were subjected to sexual exploitation or abuse on digital platforms in a single year, with most cases occurring on social media, according to a new report by Unicef.
The report estimated that more than one in five children aged 12 to 17 surveyed across Africa, Asia, Latin America and Eastern Europe experienced at least one form of sexual abuse or exploitation online in the year before they were surveyed.
Roughly 15 million children in the countries surveyed were exposed to unwanted sexual content, 9 million were pressured into sexual conversations or sharing sexual images, and 4 million had sexual images shared without their consent, the report found.
The number of children subjected to this abuse globally is certain to run into many tens of millions, it said.
The research, which Unicef described as one of the largest studies of its kind, was based on national representative surveys collected between 2020 and 2025 of around 21,000 internet-using children in 21 countries, which included Kenya, Pakistan, Brazil and Serbia.
Almost 60 per cent of reported abuse occurred on social media platforms, led by Facebook, WhatsApp, Instagram, Snapchat and TikTok, while 14 per centtook place in online gaming, the report found.
A spokesperson for Meta, which owns Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram, said the surveys go as far back as 2020, before the company introduced protections Unicef recommends such as automatically defaulting teens into private accounts and preventing adults from messaging teens they are not connected to.
It added that it defines WhatsApp as a private messaging app and not a social media platform.
"While the report doesn't provide any specific evidence of abuse, we'll continue to fight child exploitation aggressively across our apps and support law enforcement in prosecuting the criminals behind it," the Meta spokesperson said.
Snapchat pointed Reuters to a blog post by Global Head of Platform Safety Jacqueline Beauchere, who said the company was actively combating online sexual extortion through proactive detection, account removals, user reporting tools and safety features designed to protect vulnerable users.
TikTok said it has built a range of safeguards to protect minors, including restricting certain features for younger users, making accounts for under-18s private by default, and using technology to detect potentially predatory behaviour.
The Unicef report said more than half the cases involved someone the child already knew, including friends, relatives or romantic partners, while 38 per cent of children first encountered the perpetrator online.
Fewer than 1 per cent of cases involving children were reported to the police, a social worker or a helpline, according to the research.
The report also highlighted growing concerns over artificial intelligence. Across nine countries where data was collected, an estimated 1.1 million children reported having AI-generated sexual images or videos created depicting them.
Children who experienced tech-facilitated sexual exploitation were around four times more likely to report suicidal thoughts or self-harm and reported significantly higher levels of anxiety than their peers, the research said.
"These experiences cause profound emotional and mental distress. Many children suffer in silence, unsure where to turn for help," Unicef executive director Catherine Russell said in a statement.
Unicef urged governments and technology companies to strengthen safety measures on digital platforms, update laws to address evolving forms of abuse including AI-generated content, and improve child protection and reporting systems.

Title: 'My husband should come home today' — Hani appeals on 10th wedding anniversary
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: "My husband should come home today. He promised to bring home an anniversary present."
That was the plea from Hani Othman, wife of senior fire officer Mohd Fakhrul Munir Mohd Isa, better known as Loe, who remains missing after floods and landslides in the Nepal-Tibet border area.
Today marks 10 years since the couple were married.
Instead of celebrating the occasion together, Hani is waiting for news of Loe.
In a Facebook post today, she recalled the activities and dreams they had planned together.
"Happy 10th wedding anniversary. 3.9.2016 to 3.9.2026. My husband should come home today. He promised to bring home an anniversary present.
"I'm nervous about what present you're going to give this year," she said.
Hani said they were due to sit for the Sijil Kemahiran Malaysia TVET examination on Sept 6 and complete a divemaster course in Pulau Tioman in October.
They also intended to climb Mount Rinjani in May next year and visit Mount Kilimanjaro the following August.
"On 6/9 we have the SKM TVET exam. In October we should complete the divemaster course in Tioman.
"In May, you have to take me to Mount Rinjani and in August we want to go to Mount Kilimanjaro," she said.
She also referred to their unfulfilled dream of reaching the summit of Mount Everest.
Hani said she had promised to train with Loe and accompany him on the climb.
"I told you, right, that we will train together and I will accompany you this time all the way to the summit of Everest.
"Your dream of reaching the summit of Everest hasn't been settled yet. Please… where are you?" she said.
Media reports previously said Hani travelled to Kathmandu on her own initiative to obtain updates on efforts to locate Loe and the others who remain uncontactable following the disaster in Nepal.
She said she wanted to be closer to the operation rather than wait for developments from Malaysia.
In an earlier Facebook post, Hani expressed hope that none of the bodies recovered was Loe or any member of the expedition.
His friends and acquaintances in Nepal are also assisting efforts to locate them.
Hani's presence in the country has been conveyed to the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu.
Loe is among the Malaysians still uncontactable following the flash floods.
They are believed to have been in a valley when the flooding occurred.
Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division deputy director Mohd Sani Harul was among those reported missing during the same expedition.

Title: Shooting injures two police officers, others in Minneapolis
Article:
WASHINGTON: Several people were shot Wednesday, including two police officers in the northern US city of Minneapolis, officials said.
"The Minneapolis Police Department is on the scene of a shooting... involving multiple victims, including two police officers," the city said in a statement.
Hennepin Healthcare, which runs a local hospital, said it had taken in seven patients from the shooting and that one had died.
Governor Tim Walz asked the public to "pray for Minnesota," while FBI Director Kash Patel said his agents were responding.

Title: Stepfather arrested over alleged rape, sexual assault of 13-year-old girl in Besut
Article:
BESUT: Police have detained a 40-year-old man to assist in investigations involving the rape and sexual assault of his 13-year-old stepdaughter.
Deputy district police chief Deputy Superintendent Md Sani Md Salleh said police received a report regarding the case earlier yesterday.
Following the report, police arrested the man at 11.50am at a village here.
"A urine test conducted on the suspect came back positive for methamphetamine.
"The case is being investigated under Section 376(3) of the Penal Code and Section 14(d) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017," he said in a statement yesterday.
If convicted under Section 376(3) of the Penal Code, the suspect faces a maximum prison sentence of 30 years and at least 10 strokes of the rotan.
For offences under Section 14(d) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, he faces up to 20 years' imprisonment and caning.
Sani added that the suspect will be brought to the Besut magistrate's court today for a remand application.

Title: TGS TW quits as auditor for 10 Bursa firms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Audit firm TGS TW PLT has resigned as external auditor for at least 10 companies listed on Bursa Malaysia across the Main, ACE and LEAP Markets, in a sweeping move that comes just months after regulatory penalties were imposed on two of the firm's partners.
The affected companies include one Main Market-listed company, five on the ACE Market and four on the LEAP Market.
In separate filings on Tuesday, the companies said they had received formal written notices dated Aug 28 from TGS TW informing them of the firm's resignation.
TGS TW cited internal portfolio realignment and resource allocation decisions as the stated reason for stepping down.
The boards of the affected companies said they were not aware of any other matters or unresolved audit issues that required disclosure to shareholders.
They are now seeking replacement auditors and will make further announcements once the new appointments are finalised.
As of July 31, the Securities Commission Malaysia's (SC) register listed five registered individual auditors attached to TGS TW, namely, Lian Jat Meang, Lim Ge Ru, Tan Lea Ling, Tan Tian Wooi and Teoh Chey Yeat.
The latest resignations come after the Audit Oversight Board (AOB) of the SC imposed sanctions on two individual auditors from TGS TQ on June 23, 2026.
According to information published on the SC's website, Tan Tian Wooi, the engagement partner for a public interest entity audit, was fined RM50,000 after the AOB found deficiencies in audit procedures and the gathering of sufficient audit evidence across several critical areas.
These included the basis for the audit opinion, intangible assets, revenue recognition, cost of sales, and the review of trade payables at a major overseas subsidiary operating across multiple locations.
Lim Ge Ru, the engagement quality control reviewer for the same audit, was fined RM25,000 for failing to adequately review the conclusions reached in the same high-risk areas.
Both auditors were found to have breached AOB registration conditions and violated International Standards on Auditing.
However, none of the affected companies has disclosed any link between the regulatory sanctions and TGS TW's latest resignations.
The AOB's enforcement actions were also taken against the two individual auditors and not against TGS TW as a firm.

Title: Woman seeks help to verify if rescued man is missing Malaysian climber
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Malaysian woman has appealed for help to verify whether a man pictured among those rescued from the Nepal flood disaster is her missing younger brother.
The woman, who uses the handle asm aliza11 on Threads, shared photos from a rescue operation in Rasuwa showing several survivors being brought to safety.
She said one of the men in the photographs appeared to resemble her brother, Zaki.
"The first picture looks like my brother. If anyone is there, could you please cross-check? My brother is Zaki," she wrote.
However, it has yet to be confirmed whether the man pictured is Zaki or whether he is among the foreigners rescued so far.
According to a post by langtangvalley.nepal, a total of 3,021 people have been rescued from flood-affected areas in Rasuwa, including 338 foreigners, with search and rescue operations still ongoing.
Three Malaysian climbers were reported missing following flash floods and landslides along the Nepal-Tibet border last Wednesday.
They were identified as Muhammad Muhaimin Azhad Noor Hadi, 27, Muhammad Adib Haikal Awang Mansor, 27, and Muhammad Zaki Othman, 29, who lost contact while trekking in the Langtang Valley.

Title: Girlfriend dies in hospital after alleged beating, man held
Article:
PENAMPANG: A 41-year-old man has been arrested following the death of his girlfriend, who was allegedly beaten after a dispute between them.
The 44-year-old victim was brought unconscious by ambulance to the Queen Elizabeth I Hospital (HQEI) in Kota Kinabalu on Aug 31.
However, she was confirmed dead later that night while receiving treatment at the hospital.
District police chief Superintendent Sammy Newton said following the incident, the Penampang Criminal Investigation Department (CID) launched an investigation and subsequently detained the local man.
"Initial investigations revealed that the incident was suspected to have stemmed from a misunderstanding between the victim and the suspect before the woman was allegedly beaten," he said in a statement yesterday.
Sammy said the Penampang CID, in collaboration with the Forensic Division (D10) of the Sabah police headquarters CID, also inspected the scene of the incident.
He added that several items of physical evidence and related samples were seized for forensic analysis.
"The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder, and investigations are ongoing.
Those with information can contact the investigating officer, Assistant Superintendent Mohd Hairie Awang Akub at 016-8032849 or report to the nearest police station.

Title: Ringgit opens higher against US dollar ahead of OPR decision
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher against the US dollar on Thursday as investors awaited Bank Negara Malaysia's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) decision on the overnight policy rate (OPR) later today.
At 8am, the local currency rose to 4.0385/0455 against the greenback from Wednesday's close of 4.0435/0475.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the focus today would be on the MPC's OPR decision, with the central bank widely expected to keep the policy rate unchanged at 2.75 per cent.
Meanwhile, Mohd Afzanizam said the US Dollar Index fell 0.12 per cent to 99.555 points ahead of the US nonfarm payrolls data due on Friday.
He said market attention in recent days had centred on Federal Reserve (Fed) chair Kevin Warsh's speech at the Jackson Hole Symposium last Friday, with his remarks on elevated inflation interpreted as a signal that a rate hike could be on the table at the Fed's Federal Open Market Committee meeting in mid-September.
"This has led to a correction in the value of the ringgit against the US dollar," he added.
As such, Mohd Afzanizam expects the ringgit to improve slightly today, although it is likely to remain in a narrow trading range.
Against a basket of major currencies, the ringgit strengthened against the British pound to 5.4443/4537 from Wednesday's 5.4527/4581 and edged up against the euro to 4.6782/6863 from 4.6787/6834.
However, the local note weakened against the Japanese yen to 2.5411/5456 from 2.5294/5321.
The ringgit traded mixed against regional currencies.
It edged up against the Indonesian rupiah to 227.3/227.8 from 227.6/227.9 and rose against the Philippine peso to 6.45/6.47 from 6.46/6.47 at Wednesday's close.
However, it declined against the Singapore dollar to 3.1764/1822 from 3.1739/1773 and fell against the Thai baht to 12.1660/1926 from Wednesday's close of 12.1321/1488.

Title: IMF's Georgieva says rising bond yields threaten progress on developing country debt
Article:
ASHEVILLE, North Carolina: Ballooning debt and rising bond yields in advanced economies are threatening to undo developing and low-income countries' progress in reining in their own debts, International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva told Reuters.
Georgieva said in an interview late on Tuesday on the sidelines of a G20 finance leaders meeting in North Carolina that bond yields are being driven upwards by higher overall debt levels, continued inflation pressures from the still-closed Strait of Hormuz and competition for capital from AI-related debt issuance.
"This is not just a low-income developing countries problem," Georgieva said. "High debt levels in advanced economies, combined with stubborn inflation, could lead to debt service costs going up for everybody, including for the low income, for the emerging markets and developing economies."
US government bonds have sold off in recent weeks, pushing the 30-year US Treasury yield to near two-decade highs.
In 2022, the IMF estimated that 60 per cent of low-income countries were in debt distress or at high risk of distress, but Georgieva said this had since eased because of strong fiscal policy reforms with support from international institutions and official creditors.
That progress is now at risk, she added.
"We need to remember that some of the emerging market economies have worked very hard to gain market credibility and compress spreads.
That could be erased by a lift in debt service costs, by the increase in yields globally by advanced economies," Georgieva said.
Nonetheless, she said that debt markets were functioning in an orderly manner and expressed optimism that there was broad consensus among G20 finance ministers and central bank governors on improving the G20 Common Framework for debt restructuring and speeding up relief for countries experiencing debt distress.
SENEGAL TEST CASE ON DEBT
During a G20 session on sovereign debt restructuring, the IMF announced it had reached a staff-level agreement with Senegal for a US$2.2 billion three-year loan package, conditional on Senegal's seeking Common Framework debt treatment.
The Common Framework was launched during the COVID-19 pandemic in November 2020 to bring official and private creditors together to agree on restructuring crisis-hit countries' debt.
But it took years to achieve debt workouts for the first two debtor countries, Chad and Zambia, amid disagreements over how any losses would be shared among private creditors, international institutions including the IMF and World Bank, and their largest lender, China.
An improved process agreed to in May aims to streamline debt restructurings by laying out required steps and linking them with an IMF financial support agreement, which also requires a memorandum of understanding with the creditors committee on the main terms.
Georgieva said if the new process works well and quickly for a Senegal debt workout, it will encourage more countries to seek similar debt treatments.
"We have the next case," she said of Senegal. "Let's make it work, and you can be sure that the Fund would be very relentlessly pursuing speedy completion."

Title: PKR youth chief warns overspending could undermine country's finances
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim has warned that spending beyond approved allocations is inappropriate and could undermine the country's financial position.
"How can the money be enough when spending exceeds the allocations that have been set? We are living beyond our means. This is how a country is ruined," said Kamil, who is also political secretary to the finance minister, in a Facebook post yesterday.
He was reacting to statements by Treasury secretary-general Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican, who revealed today that the Rural and Regional Development Ministry had consistently overspent on rural road projects over the past several years.
Johan said the ministry's actual expenditure in 2023 amounted to RM1.8 billion compared with its approved allocation of RM1.1 billion, while in 2024, expenditure reached RM2 billion against an allocation of RM1.3 billion.
The overspending continued in 2025, with actual expenditure touching RM2.3 billion against an approved allocation of RM1.6 billion.
For 2026, the approved allocation was RM2.1 billion, with actual expenditure already hitting RM1.9 billion as of June.
Johan said the Finance Ministry is working with the ministry to address the issue, including reprioritising the ministry's allocations.

Title: 'Dangerous behaviour': FAA fines Boeing US$3.1mil over safety violations
Article:
WASHINGTON: Boeing paid a US$3.1 million fine to the US Federal Aviation Administration this year, after the agency said the planemaker had committed a series of safety violations, including actions tied to the 2024 Alaska Airlines MAX 9 mid-air emergency, the FAA told Reuters Wednesday.
The FAA said the full amount sought in September 2025 was paid by Boeing in January and had not been previously disclosed publicly. Boeing also confirmed to Reuters it paid the fine.
The FAA also said last year it was fining Boeing for interfering with safety officials' independence and said the planemaker presented for agency approval two aircraft that were not airworthy.
In 2024, the FAA said it found hundreds of quality system violations at the planemaker's 737 factory in Renton, Washington, and the 737 fuselage factory of then Boeing subcontractor Spirit AeroSystems in Wichita, Kansas, from September 2023 through February 2024.
The FAA found that a Boeing employee pressured a co-worker who was performing tasks on behalf of the FAA to sign off on a 737 MAX so the company could meet its delivery schedule, even though the co-worker had determined that the aircraft did not comply with regulatory standards.
Democratic US Senator Richard Blumenthal previously called the FAA fine inadequate, adding, "For Boeing, such fines are easily absorbed as the cost of doing business, not a meaningful deterrent to dangerous behavior."
Blumenthal previously investigated Boeing safety issues and chaired a committee when it probed the Alaska mid-air cabin blowout incident.
The panel released a report showing Boeing whistleblowers raised significant concerns about the company's manufacturing processes.
The Alaska Airlines incident, which involved a 737 MAX found missing four key bolts, badly damaged Boeing's reputation and led to a brief grounding of the MAX 9 and an FAA monthly production cap of 38 planes that was lifted in October 2025.
The FAA in July said it would allow Boeing to issue airworthiness certificates for all 737 MAX and 787 airplanes after "months of thorough data and safety review demonstrating consistent production quality."

Title: New York bans AI use for students until high school
Article:
New York bans AI use for students until high school
AFP
NEW YORK: New York is banning student use of artificial intelligence until high school, the city's mayor announced Wednesday, in a move designed to protect children's education and mental health.
The one-year restriction, which impacts nearly 600,000 public school pupils through eighth grade, will be closely watched across the United States as the city's school board is by far the largest in the country.
Only high school students – typically aged 14 and above – will be permitted to use artificial intelligence in limited pilot programs, and they will be offered biannual AI literacy classes.
Companion chatbots, designed specifically for emotional support, will be banned across all grades.
"The tech industry wants us to believe that AI-powered early education is not only inevitable, but necessary. We do not see it that way," Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement.
"Children need teachers and human connection in order to learn and grow. They need to develop skills alongside their peers, build relationships with educators and wrestle with tough problems on their own," he added.
Teachers will still be permitted to use AI for lesson planning and administrative tasks.
Throughout the 2026-2027 school year, a task force of students, teachers, parents, elected officials and industry experts will meet to assess the impact of the moratorium before publishing its findings.
"We have a responsibility to ensure that rapidly-changing technology supports our children and their learning, rather than getting in the way of it," New York Governor Kathy Hochul said Wednesday.
The new rules follow an initial framework published in March that allowed students to use AI for research, exploration and creative projects, sparking fury among many parents and teachers who considered it too lenient.
In response, the city's schools chancellor Kamar Samuels said that leaders had "missed the mark" in their communications, adding his office would review the feedback for incorporation into future rules.

Title: Gold rebounds over 1pct as US dollar, yields pull back from highs
Article:
NEW YORK: Gold bounced from a near one-month low on Wednesday as the US dollar and Treasury yields retreated from recent highs, while investors awaited US payrolls data due later this week for cues on the Federal Reserve's policy path.
Spot gold rose 1.1 per cent to US$4,376.41 an ounce by 01:57 p.m. EDT (1757 GMT), rebounding from its lowest level since Aug 7 hit earlier in the session. US gold futures for December delivery edged 0.4 per cent higher to settle at US$4,414.60.
"One of the reasons that gold has been able to move back above unchanged is we have seen a little tick down in yields for the day and that has allowed gold to bounce off some of the recent lows," said David Meger, director of metals trading at High Ridge Futures.
"Clearly, the energy complex and yields remain a major focus for the gold market moving forward."
US Treasury yields eased after touching multi-year highs earlier in the session, as oil prices eased and investors gauged the latest round of economic data.
The dollar also slipped from a near three-week peak.
Federal Reserve Bank of New York President John Williams said rising long-term bond yields are not driven by inflation fears but are instead a reflection of a solid economy.
Meanwhile, US private payroll growth came in below expectations in August, but gold prices remained largely unmoved as investors looked ahead to Friday's nonfarm payrolls report.
"ADP is unreliable and it might set the tone for non-farm, but non-farm is by far the most important one (for markets)," added Rhona O'Connell, head of market analysis at Stone X.
Traders are now pricing in a 64 per cent chance of an interest rate hike at the central bank's policy meeting this month, the CME FedWatch Tool showed.
Elsewhere, the Dutch central bank said it had transferred 86 metric tons of gold from New York and Ottawa to London over the past six months to improve tradability and bolster crisis preparedness.
Among other metals, spot silver gained 1.2 per cent to US$65.03 per ounce, platinum rose 0.9 per cent to US$1,756.39, and palladium rose 3.18 per cent to US$1,352.74.

Title: Oil settles 1pct higher, as US-Iran strikes threaten supplies
Article:
HOUSTON: Brent crude prices settled one per cent higher in a volatile session on Wednesday, driven by renewed military strikes between the United States (US) and Iran that have restricted world oil supply.
The US-Iran war is now in its seventh month, with the latest attacks representing the biggest exchange of fire between Tehran and Washington since July. US forces struck Iran's southern coast and Iran fired on American bases across the region.
Brent crude futures settled up 98 cents, or one per cent, at US$95.63 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate crude futures rose 79 cents, or 0.9 per cent, to settle at US$91.01.
Brent and WTI swung between gains of as much as US$2 a barrel and losses of US$1 a barrel throughout the session. The session highs for both benchmarks were the highest since July 24.
"The latest strikes mark a significant escalation after roughly a month of relative calm, with the US targeting Iranian radar and mine-laying capabilities and Iran retaliating against US positions across the region," Mark Schaefer, a director at brokerage Liquidity Energy, wrote in a note.
"The key concern for the oil market is whether the renewed fighting leads to another deterioration in physical flows through the region," Schaefer said.
The war began with joint US-Israeli strikes on Iranian targets in late February. Since then, Iran has effectively shut down shipping traffic in the Strait of Hormuz, a critical waterway that carried about a fifth of global oil and LNG consumed before the conflict.
Nations worldwide have been trying to limit price rises by finding other sources of supply and relying on their reserves, which have also dwindled.
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said the US attacks would further restrict traffic through the strait.
Four commodity vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz, below the 10-day average of around 13, preliminary Kpler shipping data showed on Wednesday.
Two oil tankers hit sea mines and were disabled while attempting to transit the strait, Iran's Revolutionary Guards said on Wednesday in a statement shared by state media.
Iran also added more ships it deems as non-compliant and subject to fines, confiscation or detention if they try to sail through the Strait of Hormuz, according to a government website.
However, US Secretary of Energy Chris Wright claimed on Tuesday that 17 million barrels of oil transited the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, calling it the largest volume of crude to pass through the waterway since the Iran war began.
In August, Iraq boosted its oil exports, and shipments were set to climb again in September as wide profits and Iranian approval for its tankers to pass through the Strait of Hormuz have encouraged buyers, according to industry sources and shipping data.
"While the increase in conflicts will slow transit through the Strait of Hormuz in the near term, the market has absorbed the fact that workaround crude oil supplies can still make it to the market eventually," said Dennis Kissler, senior vice-president of trading at BOK Financial.
OPEC+ is also likely to keep its oil output policy unchanged for October at a meeting on Sunday, three sources close to the matter told Reuters, as the producer group completes the unwinding of one layer of production cuts this month and turns its focus to 2027 quota negotiations.
Elsewhere, Russia carried out a heavy missile and drone attack on energy infrastructure in Ukraine's southern region of Odesa overnight, transmission system operator Ukrenergo said on Wednesday.
In the US, crude oil inventories fell by 4.5 million barrels last week, the Energy Information Administration said on Wednesday, compared with analysts' expectations in a Reuters poll for a 1.1 million-barrel draw.

Title: Japan bond yield surge puts ringgit in the spotlight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Japan's bond market is becoming a competitor for global capital again, raising the prospect of money flowing back to the country and putting pressure on the ringgit and Malaysian assets, analysts said.
The concern comes after Japan's benchmark 10-year government bond yield breached three per cent on Tuesday for the first time since 1996, offering domestic investors returns rarely seen in decades.
SPI Asset Management managing director Stephen Innes said yields at that level could give Japanese institutions greater reason to keep capital at home or repatriate some funds invested overseas.
"At a three per cent 10-year yield, some Japanese institutions have more reason to keep capital at home or bring some overseas funds back.
"I would expect this to be gradual rather than a sudden withdrawal from Malaysia. But if Japanese yields continue to rise, they become another source of competition for global capital," he told Business Times.
Japanese investors have built up vast overseas holdings over decades as ultra-low interest rates at home pushed them to seek better returns abroad.
The latest jump in yields was driven by concerns over inflation and Japan's fiscal health, as well as mounting pressure on the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to raise interest rates more aggressively.
The rise was also supported by comments from US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who signalled that he expected Tokyo and the BOJ to take action to support the weakening yen.
Innes said the ringgit could come under pressure if Malaysia's yield advantage over developed markets narrows, reducing the relative appeal of ringgit-denominated assets.
"A currency can offset that if investors expect it to remain stable or appreciate, but generally a shrinking yield advantage makes the currency less attractive," he said.
However, Innes said Malaysia's exposure to the artificial intelligence investment boom could provide some cushion for the currency.
"Malaysia has a distinct artificial intelligence advantage over many of its regional partners, and this could limit ringgit losses relative to broader Asian foreign exchange," he said.
The impact on Malaysian equities should remain relatively modest unless the global bond sell-off intensifies significantly, he added.
Higher bond yields could weigh on stock valuations by raising discount rates while making fixed-income assets more attractive relative to equities, particularly in yield-sensitive sectors.
RINGGIT PERFORMANCE
The potential headwind comes as the ringgit strengthened against the US dollar in August.
MBSB Research said the local currency gained 1.5 per cent month-on-month to end August at RM4.025 against the greenback, compared with RM4.086 at end-July.
The ringgit initially weakened in the first half of the month, touching RM4.0975, before reversing course from mid-August.
It briefly strengthened past RM4.02 towards the end of the month before closing slightly above that level.
MBSB Research said the ringgit traded largely sideways between RM4.070 and RM4.095 in early August, tracking broader movements in the US dollar.
"The dollar was initially supported by renewed geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and expectations of further Fed tightening to contain elevated inflationary pressures.
"While Malaysia's domestic economic fundamentals remained firm, the ringgit's short-term direction continued to be influenced by swings in the US dollar," it said.
The yen, meanwhile, weakened 1.5 per cent month-on-month against the US dollar in August despite support from coordinated intervention with the US.
RISKS SEEN MANAGEABLE
Tradeview Capital fund manager Neoh Jia Man said the direct impact on Malaysian government bond yields should be limited as Japan is not a major holder of Malaysian government securities.
However, the broader implications could be more significant given Japan's position as one of the world's largest holders of foreign assets.
"Japan is the world's third-largest holder of foreign assets and has consistently ranked among Malaysia's top five foreign direct investment partner countries.
"Should Japanese government bond (JGB) yields rerate to a sustainably higher level, we would likely see global discount rates move upward, which could weigh on investment expenditure into Malaysia," he said.
Neoh said persistently higher Japanese yields could have negative longer-term implications for both the ringgit and equities, particularly if they trigger an unwinding of the yen carry trade.
The carry trade typically involves investors borrowing cheaply in yen and investing the funds in higher-yielding assets elsewhere. Rising Japanese interest rates reduce the attractiveness of that strategy and could prompt some investors to unwind their positions.
"That said, the more immediate and influential driver remains the direction of US long-term interest rates, which we believe explains most of the recent rise in Japanese bond yields," Neoh said.
Areca Capital Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Danny Wong said higher Japanese yields could draw funds away from other markets as investors seek better returns at home.
However, he expects the impact on Malaysia to remain manageable given the country's underlying fundamentals and market liquidity.
"Higher rates may also discourage borrowing in yen, which could encourage a reversal of carry trades," he said.
Neoh said that, assuming no change in Bank Negara Malaysia's monetary policy or Malaysian bond yields, higher long-term JGB yields would make Japanese bonds relatively more attractive.
"With the 10-year JGB yield now above the three per cent level, it has become investable again, and we expect Japanese institutional investors to consider relocating capital home.
"That said, expectations of further BOJ rate hikes, uncertainty over the domestic inflation outlook and a volatile yen will likely discourage those investors from moving into Japanese bonds in a big way immediately. Hence, the process will likely be gradual," he said.
Malaysian and other emerging-market assets could nevertheless face greater volatility in the near term if concerns over an unwinding of the yen carry trade intensify, Neoh added.
MALAYSIAN BOND MARKET
Malaysia's ringgit bond and sukuk market, meanwhile, reached a record RM2.388 trillion in outstanding issuances in August, according to BIX Malaysia.
This was RM26 billion, or 1.10 per cent, higher than RM2.362 trillion in July, reflecting continued growth in the domestic fixed-income market.
Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields rose across all tenors during the month.
The three-year MGS yield increased six basis points (bps) to 3.36 per cent, while the five-year and seven-year yields climbed 12 bps and 15 bps to 3.61 per cent and 3.80 per cent, respectively.
At the longer end of the curve, the benchmark 10-year MGS yield rose 17 bps to 3.87 per cent from 3.70 per cent in July.

Title: Why internal audit fails
Article:
Internal audit is intended to provide independent assurance, identify risks, evaluate controls and help organisations improve governance and performance.
Yet, despite having an internal audit function, many organisations continue to experience fraud, control failures, regulatory breaches, operational problems and strategic surprises.
The problem is often not the existence of internal audit but how internal audit is positioned, managed and executed.
An internal audit function can fail even when it has competent auditors, because weaknesses in independence, risk assessment, communication, skills, culture and follow-up undermine its effectiveness.
Lack of Independence
Independence is fundamental to effective internal auditing. Internal auditors must be sufficiently independent from the activities they audit.
Problems arise when the chief audit executive reports primarily to management rather than having meaningful access to the audit committee or board. Auditors may then become reluctant to challenge senior executives or report sensitive findings.
An internal audit function that is afraid to tell management uncomfortable truths cannot provide effective assurance.
Auditing What Is Easy Rather Than What Is Risky
One of the most common failures is focusing on routine and low-risk areas rather than significant organisational risks.
Auditors may repeatedly audit expenses, procurement documentation or compliance checklists because these areas are familiar and relatively easy to audit.
Meanwhile, major risks involving strategy, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, third-party relationships, financial reporting, business continuity, culture or management override may receive inadequate attention.
Effective internal audit should be risk-based, not merely activity-based.
Poor Audit Planning
Weak audit planning can cause internal audit resources to be directed toward the wrong priorities.
An annual audit plan should be based on a proper understanding of the organisation's objectives, risk profile, emerging risks, regulatory environment and control weaknesses.
If the audit plan is simply rolled forward from previous years, internal audit may continue examining yesterday's risks while missing tomorrow's threats.
Excessive Focus on Compliance
Compliance is important, but internal audit should not become merely a compliance-checking function.
An audit that confirms whether policies were followed without considering whether those policies and controls actually manage the underlying risks provides limited value.
For example, an auditor may confirm that procurement forms were properly completed without asking whether the organisation is obtaining value for money, whether suppliers are appropriately selected or whether conflicts of interest exist.
Internal audit should examine not only "Were the rules followed?" but also "Are the rules and controls achieving their intended objectives?"
Weak Understanding of the Business
Auditors who do not understand the organisation's business model may struggle to identify significant risks.
Understanding the business means knowing how the organisation makes money, delivers services, interacts with customers, depends on suppliers, uses technology and creates value.
Without business knowledge, auditors can become overly focused on transactions and documentation rather than understanding the bigger picture.
Inadequate Auditor Skills
The risks facing organisations are becoming increasingly complex. Internal auditors may need knowledge of data analytics, cybersecurity, technology, financial reporting, fraud, risk management, sustainability, artificial intelligence and regulatory developments.
A traditional audit skill set may no longer be sufficient.
Internal audit fails when it continues using yesterday's methods to examine tomorrow's risks.
Continuous professional development is therefore essential.
Poor Root Cause Analysis
Another major weakness is identifying symptoms rather than causes.
For example, an audit may report that several payments were made without proper approval. However, simply recommending that staff "comply with the approval procedure" does not address why the problem occurred.
The real cause might be inadequate system controls, unclear authority limits, unrealistic processing deadlines or management override.
Without identifying root causes, the same problem is likely to recur.
Weak Audit Reports
A technically correct audit report can still fail if nobody understands why the findings matter.
Reports sometimes contain lengthy descriptions of procedures, excessive technical language and numerous minor findings while failing to explain the business impact.
A strong audit report should clearly communicate:
What happened? Why did it happen? What is the risk? Why does it matter? What needs to change? Who is responsible?
Senior management and the board need meaningful insights, not simply lists of control deficiencies.
Failure to Challenge Management
Internal auditors must be willing to challenge assumptions.
If auditors accept management explanations without sufficient evidence, they may become overly dependent on management's perspective.
Professional scepticism is particularly important when auditing areas involving significant estimates, unusual transactions, related parties, aggressive targets or potential conflicts of interest.
Being professional does not mean being confrontational. It means being prepared to ask difficult questions.
Poor Follow-Up
An audit is not successful simply because a report has been issued.
If management agrees to corrective actions but nobody verifies implementation, findings can remain unresolved for years.
Effective follow-up should determine whether agreed actions were actually implemented and whether they have adequately reduced the underlying risk.
Repeated findings are often a sign that internal audit's recommendations or management's corrective actions are ineffective.
Measuring the Wrong Things
Internal audit performance is sometimes measured by the number of audits completed, reports issued or findings identified.
These measures can encourage auditors to focus on activity rather than impact.
A better question is whether internal audit has helped the organisation identify significant risks, strengthen controls, prevent losses and improve governance.

Title: Oil rush adds RM590mil to Hengyuan's market value in two days
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd has added about RM590 million to its market value in just two trading days, emerging as the biggest winner from a renewed rush into oil and gas stocks.
The refiner's shares have jumped 99 sen, or 50.77 per cent, from RM1.95 last Friday to RM2.94 at Wednesday's close, lifting its market capitalisation from about RM1.17 billion to RM1.76 billion.
Bursa Malaysia was closed on Monday for the National Day public holiday.
When trading resumed on Tuesday, Hengyuan hit its daily limit, soaring 58 sen, or 29.74 per cent, to RM2.53 as investors piled into energy counters amid renewed hostilities between the United States (US) and Iran.
The two-day burst is the latest chapter in what has already been a remarkable year for the refiner.
A REMARKABLE RUN
Hengyuan began 2026 at just 77 sen. At RM2.88, the stock has gained RM2.11, or 274 per cent, since the start of the year.
But its meteoric rise has been anything but a straight line.
In March, Business Times reported that Hengyuan had emerged as Bursa Malaysia's biggest winner from an earlier crude oil rally after its shares soared 85.71 per cent in just one week, from 91 sen to RM1.69.
That rally alone added about RM468 million to its market value.
No fundamental analyst currently tracks Hengyuan, but RHB Research in a July 14 technical note said the stock could hit RM1.50 after breaking above RM1.25. It has since more than doubled from that breakout level.
The latest rally comes as crude prices climb on fears that escalating US-Iran hostilities could further disrupt supplies from the Middle East.
Brent crude futures rose 40.5 cents, or 0.43 per cent, to US$95.60 a barrel at press time yesterday, after jumping more than US$4 on Tuesday in their biggest daily gain since July 24.
The escalation has again put the Strait of Hormuz in the spotlight. The waterway, through which about one-fifth of global oil consumption passed before the conflict, has effectively been closed to commercial shipping by Iran.
The renewed appetite for energy stocks also comes as analysts turn more upbeat on the sector's underlying prospects.
Hong Leong Investment Bank Bhd (HLIB) expects Malaysia's oil and gas sector to gather momentum on a recovery in upstream earnings, improving order flows for oil and gas services and equipment (OGSE) companies and sustained demand for energy infrastructure.
The research house maintained its "Overweight" call on the sector, with Dialog Group Bhd its top pick at a target price of RM2.52.
HLIB expects Petroliam Nasional Bhd (Petronas) to step up upstream capital expenditure (capex) in financial year 2027 (FY27), potentially breathing new life into domestic OGSE activity after a softer first half of this year.
"We believe Petronas' upstream capex will recover in FY27, alongside rising energy security investments across the region," it said in a Sept 1 note.
Upstream spending accounted for just 21 per cent of Petronas' total capex in the first half of FY26, well below the 43 per cent to 52 per cent range seen between FY19 and FY25.
In absolute terms, however, upstream capex was broadly stable at RM9 billion against RM8.6 billion a year earlier.
HLIB said softer domestic activity and slower work-order issuance had weighed on Malaysian upstream service providers in the first half, resulting in weaker rig and vessel utilisation as well as subdued maintenance, construction and modification activities.
Among those affected were Dayang Enterprise Holdings Bhd, Perdana Petroleum Bhd, Keyfield International Bhd, Velesto Energy Bhd and Deleum Bhd.
BEYOND THE OIL RALLY
A recovery in Petronas spending could therefore provide another leg of support for the sector beyond the current oil-price rally.
HLIB also sees energy security emerging as a longer-term investment theme, particularly for storage, pipelines and other infrastructure.
It said Dialog was well placed to ride that wave, with scope to add four million to five million cubic metres of storage capacity on about 242.8ha of buffer land in Pengerang.
The research house maintained its Brent forecasts at US$80 a barrel for 2026 and US$75 for 2027, but said risks were increasingly tilted to the upside if the regional conflict worsens.
Persistent disruption at the Strait of Hormuz could push Brent towards US$90 a barrel in the near term, HLIB said.
That level has already been surpassed, with Brent trading above US$95 on Wednesday.
HLIB said fewer than 10 vessels were currently being tracked through the strait, compared with about 130 to 140 a day before the war.
"Further war escalation, attacks that halt transit through the Red Sea, and continued disruption at Hormuz could tighten regional export capacity further and drive Brent materially above our base-case assumptions," it said.
RIDING THE WAVE
Against that backdrop, Hengyuan was not alone in riding the renewed wave of interest in energy stocks.
The Bursa Malaysia Energy Index jumped 12.11 points, or 1.5 per cent, to 801.95 at closing yesterday, extending its advance for a second session.
Velesto Energy Bhd rose 1.5 sen, or 6.5 per cent, to 24.5 sen, while Hibiscus Petroleum Bhd climbed as much as 9.25 per cent to RM2.49 before surrendering its gains to close flat at RM2.25.
The broader market was little changed, with the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI adding 8.2 points, or 0.5 per cent, to 1,708.74.
Beyond energy, the Industrial Products and Services sector also lent support to the benchmark, led by Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd.
The petrochemical producer rose 29 sen, or 7.1 per cent, to RM4.36, giving it a market capitalisation of about RM34.88 billion.

Title: Wall Street ends higher as stocks reclaim some shine
Article:
NEW YORK: Wall Street advanced on Wednesday, notching a partial rebound from a three-day losing streak as investors searched for deals among stocks and sectors that might have been oversold amid recent risk-off moves.
All three major US stock indexes gained ground, with the small-cap Russell 2000 outperforming its larger-cap peers, rising 1.1 per cent.
On the sector level, airlines, gold and silver miners and regional banks were the frontrunners, while software and services, seen as potential victims of AI disruption, underperformed on the day.
The Philadelphia SE Semiconductor Index, which has powered much of the stock market's gains so far this year but has lost nearly one-fourth of its value since late June, was on the rise, with chipmaker Broadcom expected to deliver second-quarter results after the bell.
Nvidia, the chipmaker at the forefront of the AI wave, rose 3.2 per cent, while Micron and Qualcomm gained 2.4 per cent and 2.0 per cent, respectively.
"The war is continuing longer than anyone hoped, and when it ends, energy will cool and inflation won't be as much of an issue," said Lauren Cassidy, chief investment officer at Founders 100 ETF in Dallas.
At the same time, we just had a record earnings season, with wonderful fundamentals being driven by the accelerating adoption of AI."
"AI adoption is still in the very early innings and it's just now accelerating," Cassidy added. "We could see exponential growth from here."
The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 295.01 points, or 0.56 per cent, to 53,061.89, the S&P 500 gained 35.16 points, or 0.46 per cent, to 7,666.63 and the Nasdaq Composite gained 118.05 points, or 0.45 per cent, to 26,217.83.
Of the 11 major sectors in the S&P 500, materials enjoyed the biggest percentage gains, while real estate was the sole percentage loser.
Hardware firm Dell advanced 15.8 per cent after raising its annual profit and revenue forecast.
Jack Daniel's maker Brown-Forman rose 3.9 per cent following its quarterly profit beat.
Uber Technologies gained 1.6 per cent after the rideshare app announced it will lay off about 10 per cent of its staff.
BOND SELLOFF STILL KEEPING MARKETS ON EDGE
Keeping gains in check, the market-shaking global bond sell-off continued, fuelled by fears over inflation and mushrooming government debt, and compounded by escalating tensions in the Middle East, which have put upward pressure on energy prices.
The US and Iran ramped up their attacks in the biggest exchange of airstrikes since July, dousing hopes of a return to the negotiating table and raising the likelihood that protracted hostilities could result in systemic inflation and force central bank leaders to raise borrowing costs.
In economics, payrolls processor ADP reported fewer-than-expected private sector job adds in August, while new orders for core capital goods were downwardly revised, signalling a potential softening in US corporate spending plans.
International trade, second-quarter labour costs/productivity, and services PMI are among the economic reports on Thursday's docket.
Advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.78-to-1 ratio on the New York Stock Exchange. There were 150 new highs and 290 new lows on the NYSE.
On the Nasdaq, 3,102 stocks rose and 1,679 fell as advancing issues outnumbered decliners by a 1.85-to-1 ratio.
The S&P 500 posted 12 new 52-week highs and 10 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 58 new highs and 135 new lows.
Volume on US exchanges was 14.75 billion shares, compared with the 15.19 billion average for the full session over the last 20 trading days.

Title: Trump 'happy' Prince Harry and Meghan have left US
Article:
WASHINGTON: President Donald Trump said Wednesday he was glad Prince Harry and Meghan Markle had left the United States – though adding that if he were part of the British royal family he would not have taken them back.
"I'm happy about it. I was not a fan," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office a week after the prince and his American wife moved back to Britain from their home in Montecito, California.
"I thought they treated the royal family with great disrespect. I didn't like it. I didn't like the way she acted. I thought she was terribly disrespectful to the Queen, to King Charles."
The A-list celebrity couple is now settling in back in Britain, six years after they left for the United States amid acrimony over their bitter criticisms of the royal family.
Harry appeared to have mended relations with his father, King Charles III, who is battling cancer, during more recent UK visits. But Harry reportedly remains estranged from his brother, heir-to-the-throne, Prince William, and William's wife Catherine.
Trump, who has previously criticized actress Meghan on a number of occasions, said he wouldn't have been so forgiving.
"Maybe I'm different. I wouldn't have taken him back, right? If I were the royal family, I would not have taken them back," said Trump.

Title: ADI equips workers with industry-ready skills - HR Ministry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Workplace-based training is gaining ground among businesses, with 1,366 companies,including 677 small and medium enterprises (SMEs), now participating in the government's Academy in Industry (ADI) programme.
Deputy Human Resources Minister Datuk Khairul Firdaus Akbar Khan said ADI's work-based learning approach allowed participants to gain practical experience while being trained according to industry requirements.
He said the programme combined classroom learning with workplace training, enabling participants to familiarise themselves with actual company technology, systems and processes.
"Participants not only gain theoretical knowledge but also real workplace experience.
"This enables employers to reduce the adjustment period for new workers, improve productivity earlier and reduce the need for additional training after recruitment," he told the New Straits Times.
Khairul said ADI's train-and-place approach had helped improve workforce readiness as training was developed and implemented together with industries based on the National Occupational Skills Standard.
ADI uses two main approaches, namely ADI Apprenticeship and ADI Employment.
Under ADI Apprenticeship, jobseekers, including vulnerable groups, undergo 20 to 30 per cent classroom training at training centres, while the remaining 70 to 80 per cent is conducted at participating companies.
The government provides an incentive of RM1,000 per apprentice, comprising RM500 as a training allowance, RM300 for training centres, and RM200 for participating companies.
Meanwhile, ADI Employment targets new and existing workers aged 18 and above, enabling participants to receive salaries at the minimum wage while undergoing workplace-based training.
Participants receive a government incentive of RM2,500 for the programme, while companies receive RM700 for each participant trained and training centres receive RM900.
Khairul said companies participating in ADI had reported benefits, including increased productivity through a more competent workforce, and lower recruitment and training costs.
He said the programme also contributed to higher participant absorption as permanent employees and reduced turnover as workers became familiar with company operations.
He said the government would continue strengthening ADI through financial incentives, training assistance, simplified participation processes and greater engagement with industry associations and SMEs.
"By encouraging collaboration and sharing of facilities and expertise between companies and training providers, the approach aims to reduce implementation burdens on SMEs while ensuring they can develop skilled workers sustainably," he said.

Title: ADI helps companies turn experienced workers into future leaders
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Years of experience can teach a worker how to get a job done, but moving up often requires a different skill set.
For Schott Glass Malaysia Sdn Bhd, the focus is on helping existing employees build on what they already know by giving them the skills to solve problems, improve processes and eventually lead others.
The company joined the government's Academy in Industry (ADI) programme to upskill its workforce, allowing employees to strengthen their competencies in their existing roles
Schott Glass Malaysia human resources manager Suhaila Mustapha Kamal said this was particularly valuable for workers who already had operational experience but needed to strengthen their competencies before moving into bigger roles.
"ADI allowed us to enhance and structure their skills so that they are better prepared to take on greater responsibilities.
"At the same time, we also want to bridge the gap between what employees do every day and the competencies they need to develop in their careers," she said.
Building on what they know
Suhaila said about 80 per cent of their ADI programme involved workplace activities, with the remaining 20 per cent focused on theory.
This means participants can apply what they learn almost immediately, including in areas such as lean manufacturing, 5S, safety, quality and problem-solving.
The programme also incorporates training within industry elements, including job instruction, job methods, job relations and problem solving.
For Schott, these elements are particularly useful because employees are expected not only to know how to perform a task but also to teach and guide others on their teams.
Suhaila said employees understood the company's operations, systems and working environment, allowing the company to build on that experience instead of starting again with a new hire.
In a way, she said the programme also motivated employees, as they could see that the company was serious about investing in their development.
"I think the advantage of ADI is that we can develop our own talent.
"The participants are already working and understand the operations, so we do not start from zero.
"We take the experience they already have and add the knowledge and skills they need to grow," she said.
The programme also offers a way for small and medium enterprises (SMEs) to address one of their biggest workforce challenges — finding people with the right skills who can quickly adapt to their operations.
Small and Medium Enterprises Association of Malaysia (Samenta) president Datuk William Ng said ADI served as an important bridge between industry needs and the skills available in the labour market.
He said SMEs often struggle to find workers immediately equipped to operate machinery, understand production processes and meet business requirements.
"ADI addresses the structural disconnect between standard institutional education and real-world operations by embedding training directly into active industrial environments.
"Rather than waiting years for fresh graduates who still require significant retraining, ADI empowers SMEs to upskill candidates on the exact equipment, systems, and workflows used daily," he said.
Ng said SMEs that participated in work-based learning programmes under the Malaysia Productivity Corporation, including the precursor to ADI, had reported improvements in productivity and employee retention.
By embedding training in the workplace, he said workers could achieve operational competency faster, reducing adjustment periods and minimising disruptions to businesses.
He said employees were also more likely to remain with companies when they saw clear pathways for technical career progression through industry-recognised certifications and workplace experience.
"While it cannot single-handedly solve macro manpower shortages, it serves as a targeted solution to bridge critical skills gaps and shorten initial onboarding times," he said.
Making it easier for more businesses
Ng noted that more could be done to bring the programme to SMEs, many of which may have fewer resources to dedicate to training.
He suggested streamlining applications through a dedicated low-bureaucracy portal, as well as introducing co-funding mechanisms or tax incentives to help SMEs offset the costs of training and mentoring workers.
Ng said greater outreach was also needed, particularly in sub-urban regions where smaller businesses remained unaware of such programmes or assumed they were only targeted at large manufacturers.
Suhaila similarly said greater awareness and the sharing of experiences by companies already participating in ADI could encourage more employers to come on board.
She said additional support through incentives, implementation guidance and advisory services could also help SMEs with smaller human resources and learning and development teams.
"To me, ADI is actually not just a training programme. It's a way for companies to develop their own employees while meeting their operational needs.
"Ultimately, we do not just want workers with qualifications. We want workers who know, can do and can lead others," she said.

Title: 5,000 Dropbox accounts hacked
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
SAN FRANCISCO: Dropbox said on Tuesday around 5,000 accounts were compromised last month, with hackers viewing and downloading content stored on the cloud-storage platform.
Some Dropbox users received an email from the company on Monday notifying them that their accounts have been accessed without authorisation between Aug 4 and 21, Dropbox confirmed after Bloomberg News reported the hack earlier in the day.
Hackers accessed files in fewer than a third of the compromised accounts, the company said.
Shares of Dropbox fell around 2.4 per cent in extended trading on Tuesday.
Dropbox said it identified unauthorised access affecting accounts linked to a Lenovo ID that did not have its two-factor authentication enabled, prompting the company to terminate all sessions authenticated through a Lenovo ID.
The company has removed any links between Lenovo IDs and Dropbox accounts, and changed its systems so that users must enter their Dropbox password before accessing an account through Lenovo.
Dropbox said it had reported the incident to data protection regulators.
Lenovo identified a "legacy integration" between Lenovo ID and Dropbox that "could be used to improperly authenticate certain Dropbox accounts".
The company said its own customers were not affected and that an investigation was ongoing. — REUTERS

Title: Black bass rediscovered in Penang
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
GEORGE TOWN: The rediscovery of a black bass in Penang after 15 years could provide fresh insight into the state's river and estuary ecosystems, while raising questions about how the species reached the area.
The fish is locally known as ikan kanai or tembaring, and is scientifically identified as Lutjanus goldiei.
Fisherman Khoirul Anuar Md Akhir, 58, caught the 4.6kg fish on National Day Eve.
The Penang Fisheries Department said the catch was significant as local fishermen had not reported seeing the species in the state for about 15 years.
Universiti Sains Malaysia (USM) ichthyologist Associate Professor Dr Khaironizam Md Zain said the finding was significant for another reason as well — Penang lies considerably outside the species' previously known distribution.
He said L. goldiei was generally found in freshwater and brackish rivers and estuarine habitats, particularly in southern New Guinea and Sungai Kinabatangan in Sabah.
"Its occurrence in Penang, therefore, represents an important geographical range extension, although one fish alone may not be enough to confirm an established population.
"It is an interesting rediscovery."
Khaironizam said further sampling and surveys were needed to determine whether the species had established a resident population in Penang.
He said one possibility was that the fish had escaped from nearby fish cages, where it could have been unintentionally reared alongside other snapper species.
"Natural dispersal cannot be ruled out, particularly if changes in environmental conditions or oceanographic events had helped the species move beyond its known range."
Khaironizam said genetic analysis, together with surveys of nearby aquaculture facilities and natural habitats, could help determine where the fish came from.
"The latest catch can mean the species had been present in Penang for some time, but remained undetected because of its low abundance or limited sampling.
"If further studies confirm that an established population has existed in Penang, or elsewhere in waters off Peninsular Malaysia, the rediscovery would be particularly significant for understanding the species' distribution and biogeography."
The finding could also provide an encouraging, albeit limited, signal about Penang's aquatic environment, he noted.
Khaironizam said the species depended on healthy rivers, estuaries, mangroves and good connectivity between freshwater and marine environments.
"Its presence highlights the importance of protecting mangroves, maintaining river-estuary connectivity, preserving water quality and conserving natural fish habitats."
However, he cautioned against treating a single catch as proof that Penang's ecosystem was completely healthy.
Instead, the discovery should encourage continued monitoring of fish diversity and habitat conditions across the state.

Title: Maltese tycoon acquitted of masterminding reporter's murder
Article:
VALETTA: A Maltese court on Wednesday acquitted tycoon Yorgen Fenech of orchestrating the brutal murder in 2017 of investigative reporter Daphne Caruana Galizia, which brought down a government and drew global condemnation.
The wealthy businessman had stood accused of masterminding the car-bomb killing of 53-year-old Caruana Galizia.
Caruana Galizia's family said in a statement that Fenech's acquittal was "denying her the justice she deserves."
Dubbed a "one-woman WikiLeaks", Caruana Galizia had exposed corruption at the highest level in the country, shining a spotlight on murky links between Malta's business and political elites.
Her slaying sparked outrage around the world and put Malta, the European Union's smallest member state, in the spotlight over its apparent rule-of-law failings.
The killing also led to a political crisis, and the resignation of then-premier Joseph Muscat in January 2020 after widespread anger and mass protests over his perceived efforts to protect friends and allies from the investigation.
A two-year public inquiry published in July 2021 concluded that the state should "shoulder responsibility" for the murder due to the "atmosphere of impunity" the government had created.
Fenech, a tycoon whose business interests spanned the energy and tourism sectors, was arrested on his yacht in 2019 as he tried to sail out of Malta after a middleman in the murder was offered a pardon to identify those involved.
Prosecutors had accused Fenech of ordering the journalist to be killed because she was on the brink of publishing a compromising article about his uncle.
Five people have been convicted so far in relation to the murder for supplying the explosives and carrying out the killing.
In June 2025, Robert Agius and Jamie Vella were convicted of supplying the bomb that killed Caruana Galizia and sentenced to life in prison.
The three men who carried out the murder – brothers George and Alfred Degiorgio together with Vince Muscat – are serving prison sentences after being found guilty of their role.
The 437-page report written by a panel of three judges in 2021 found that the state had shirked its duty to protect Caruana Galizia and subjected her to personal attacks and verbal abuse from politicians.
The atmosphere created a "favourable climate" for her assassination, and there was "convincing evidence" that her killers knew they would be protected by "persons in the highest state positions."

Title: Sabah is safe for travel, US tells foreign tourists
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
KOTA KINABALU: The United States is encouraging its citizens as well as people in other countries to travel to Sabah.
US Embassy Chargé d'Affaires to Malaysia David Gamble said this followed improvements in security and a more relaxed travel status for Borneo.
"Many countries are following America's lead and reviewing their travel advisories, which reflect the increased security and how safe it is to come to Sabah.
"We want to see more tourists from around the world come here because Sabah is a fantastic place to visit," he said after launching the Freedom 250 Sabah campaign at the state library in Tanjung Aru near here.
In February, the embassy lowered its travel advisory for eastern Sabah to Level 1, advising Americans to exercise normal precaution.
However, a Level 2 advisory calling for increased caution was maintained for the islands and maritime areas off the coast.
Four months later, Japan lowered its travel advisory for coastal areas from Kudat to Tawau from Level 2 to 1, including Pulau Banggi and Pulau Balambangan.
The advisories were raised in July 2014 following a series of kidnappings for ransom.
Present at yesterday's event were Sabah Assistant Education, Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Jordan Jude Ellron and US Assistant Secretary of State for Educational and Cultural Affairs Cate Dillon.
Freedom 250 Sabah is a three-day series of programmes taking place until today to commemorate the 250th anniversary of US independence.
Tanjung Aru Library is hosting the Freedom 250 Exhibition, as well as the Fulbright Malaysia and US higher education outreach.
Science, technology, engineering and mathematics workshops are supported by energy companies McDermott and ConocoPhillips.
Also being held are an English Access Scholarship Programme and American Film Showcase workshops for emerging Sabahan filmmakers.

Title: Death toll from Nepal-China flash floods at 1,220, nearly 4,800 missing
Article:
ISLAMABAD: The death toll from last week's devastating flash floods and mudslides on the China-Nepal border has climbed to 1,220, while nearly 4,762 people, including 844 foreigners, remained missing, Anadolu Ajansi reported, citing the latest official data on Wednesday.
According to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, 1,204 bodies have been recovered in Nepal since massive flash floods hit the Himalayan country on August 26, while 301 people were injured and around 4,216 remained missing.
Nepalese authorities said around 900 personnel deployed at several hydropower stations in the country remain missing.
Authorities said 11,993 people have been rescued from the flood-hit areas, while 21,314 security personnel, including army and police, have been mobilised to assist the ongoing search and rescue operations.
Around 1.6 million people have been affected in Nepal by the flash floods, they added.
At least 16 people have been killed on the Chinese side of the border, with 546 missing, including 261 foreigners, according to Xinhua News.
Road access to the core area of the mudslide-hit Gyirong Port in Tibet, which China designates as the Xizang Autonomous Region, was restored on Wednesday after days of "round-the-clock" repair work on the damaged highway, Beijing-based Xinhua News reported.
Rescue teams, relief supplies, and some rescue equipment have entered the core rescue area via the repaired road.
A 44-member Korea Disaster Relief Team from South Korea reached Nepal Wednesday to help find the missing people. At least nine South Koreans are among the missing.
China has also sent its experts, besides drones, DNA testing devices and reagents, water-purification equipment, and lighting gear, state media reported.
India has also sent DNA analysis experts.
The disaster struck on August 26 when a glacier on Nepal's Mount Langtang Lirung fractured at an altitude of about 5,200m, triggering an ice-rock avalanche that developed into a massive debris flow and swept through valleys along the border.
The huge surge of water, along with mudslides, devastated Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Kavre, and the Kathmandu Valley in Nepal, while also burying the Gyirong border crossing with Nepal in southwestern Tibet, also known as the Xizang Autonomous Region, on the Chinese side.
– Bernama-Anadolu

Title: Gold hits 3-week low as Mideast tensions fan rate-hike fears
Article:

NEW YORK: Gold dropped to a three-week low yesterday as rising Middle East tensions drove up oil prices, stoking inflation and rate-hike fears.
At the same time, investor focus shifted to upcoming US jobs data.
Spot gold was down 0.6 per cent at US$4,304.01 per ounce by 0017 GMT, its lowest since Aug 7. Prices were headed for a fourth straight session of losses and remained below the 200-day moving average, a closely watched technical level.
US gold futures for December delivery fell one per cent to US$4,350.80.
The US dollar held firm, making dollar-denominated metals costlier for buyers using other currencies.
The US launched a barrage of airstrikes against Iran on Tuesday, prompting Iranian retaliation, in the most serious escalation in weeks.
Oil prices rose for a third straight session, while US Treasury yields advanced.
"A rebound in oil prices after renewed US-Iran tensions added to inflation concerns.
"A pricier crude could continue to tighten monetary policy expectations and drive yields higher, limiting any rebound potential for gold," said Bas Kooijman, chief executive officer and asset manager of DHF Capital SA.
Although gold is seen as an inflation hedge, higher interest rates weigh on its appeal as it offers no yield.
Traders are pricing in a 67 per cent chance of a rate hike at the Federal Reserve's policy meeting this month, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

Title: DoE to step up monitoring to curb activities worsening haze
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Department of Environment (DoE) will step up monitoring to ensure activities that could worsen the haze do not occur, particularly open burning.
DoE enforcement division director Rosli Zul said officers, together with authorised agencies, were conducting continuous monitoring and patrols involving open burning at residential areas, plantations and industrial sites, including charcoal-burning operations, as well as blasting activities at quarries.
He said the DoE had also issued letters to landowners and plantation operators, urging them to play their part in preventing activities that could worsen the Air Pollutant Index (API).
"We also constantly monitor hotspots detected through satellite images and will continue to verify whether there are fires in the affected areas to be immediately reported to the Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department for prompt extinguishing," he said when appearing on Bernama TV's Ruang Bicara programme, titled "Haze: When the Air Becomes a Threat", today.
Rosli said vehicle movements also contributed to declining air quality.
"The actual root cause (of the haze) is forest burning from neighbouring countries, worsened by hot weather coupled with the wind direction of the Southwest Monsoon. That brings (the smoke from burning) into Malaysia, but domestically, we also need to play our part so the situation does not get worse.
"Among the small steps that can be taken include making full use of public transport, if possible, to reduce reliance on private vehicles," he said.
He said the DoE would continue providing air quality information from 68 monitoring stations nationwide to help the public plan their daily activities, particularly vulnerable groups such as children and the elderly.
Based on data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), two areas in Sarawak recorded hazardous API readings this afternoon, with the Serian police headquarters recording the highest at 325.
Kuching recorded a hazardous reading of 309, while five areas recorded very unhealthy readings – Samarahan (287), Sarikei (256), Sibu (248), Sri Aman (247) and Mukah (205).
Sixteen stations recorded unhealthy readings, with Bintulu recording the highest at 192, followed by Kapit (190), Kota Kinabalu Polytechnic (178), Keningau (175) and Kota Kinabalu (173).
Other areas recording unhealthy readings were Labuan (173), Samalaju (172), Kimanis (171), ILP Miri (170), Limbang (169), Miri (166), Johan Setia (159), Putrajaya (151), Nilai (151), Sandakan (136) and Seremban (109).
