Title: Pandu Citra key platform to strengthen public service leadership - Chief secretary
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 2026 Pandu Citra Week organised by the National Institute of Public Administration (Intan) serves as an important platform for strengthening leadership within the public service, said Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar.
He said a good leader was not just responsible for managing an organisation, but must also be capable of guiding officers, recognising their potential and nurturing their development.
"With 99 Pemandu Citra Profesional Sektor Awam (public sector professional coaches) now serving as driving forces in their respective organisations, I want this coaching approach to continue to be extended to the field and adopted at every level of the department.
"Be a Pandu Citra ambassador who helps cultivate a culture of guiding, listening to and developing others in the organisation. The true measure of leadership ultimately lies not only in our own achievements, but in our ability to build more leaders after us," he said in a Facebook post yesterday.
Shamsul Azri also congratulated all award recipients recognised under the programme, including the Ministry of Health, which received the 2026 Inspirasi Pandu Citra Sektor Awam Award in the Organisation of the Year category.
In addition, Putrajaya Hospital Deputy Director of Medical Dr Mohammad Khairol Anwar Yusop was selected as the 2026 Pandu Citra Sektor Awam ambassador.
The Pandu Citra Ambassador Award was presented to Negri Sembilan Islamic Religious Council Director of Administration Muhammad Aszam Gambaris @ Watimin and Occupational Health Specialist at Tuanku Fauziah Hospital, Kangar, Perlis, Dr Muhammad Shauqi Abdul Kadir.
The 2026 Pandu Citra Week was organised to increase awareness, understanding and acceptance among public officials of the Pandu Citra approach as a method of human capital development that can strengthen leadership, improve performance and unlock individual potential towards excellence.
The programme also serves as a platform for sharing knowledge and best practices to promote wider adoption of the Pandu Citra approach in the public service.

Title: Kuching banker gets seven years’ jail, 16 lashes after draining client accounts via DuitNow
Article:
KUCHING, Sept 3 — A relationship manager with an international bank was yesterday sentenced to seven years’ jail, fined RM40 million and ordered to receive 16 strokes of the cane by the Sessions Court here after pleading guilty to fraud and money laundering charges.
Judge Iris Awen Jon sentenced Kho Yung Kang, 39, after he pleaded guilty to 16 counts of fraud under Section 420 of the Penal Code and eight counts under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (AMLA).
Kho pleaded guilty to defrauding eight senior citizens aged between 60 and 75 of RM1.58 million through a non-existent bond investment scheme, as well as committing money laundering at the bank where he worked between Sept 2022 and Feb 2024.
For each of the 16 cheating charges, Kho was sentenced to between three and four years’ jail and one stroke of the cane, with the jail terms to run concurrently from the date of his remand on May 23, 2025.
For each of the eight money laundering charges, he was sentenced to three years’ jail, with the terms to run concurrently from today, fined RM5 million or four months’ jail in default.
This brings the total sentence to seven years’ jail, a RM40 million fine and 16 strokes of the cane.
Kho failed to pay the fine.
According to the facts of the case, Kho was responsible for assisting customers with investments, including unit trusts, bonds and fixed deposits, as well as local and foreign remittances.
His modus operandi was to offer customers of the bank where he worked an investment scheme promising higher returns.
Based on the representation, Kho obtained the customers’ signatures and biometric verification, but the funds were not used for investment purposes.
Instead, the money was transferred from the customers’ accounts to third-party accounts via DuitNow, interbank transfers or Cashier’s Orders without their knowledge or consent, for Kho’s personal use.
Deputy Public Prosecutors Chuah Kai Sheng and Maryam Jamielah Ab Manaff appeared for the prosecution, while Kho was unrepresented. — Bernama

Title: Victoria Bridge incident: Father speaks on losing youngest son a year after eldest daughter
Article:
KLUANG, Sept 3 — Less than a year after mourning the loss of their eldest child, a family here is once again grieving after their youngest son died following a fall from Victoria Bridge in Enggor, Kuala Kangsar, Perak, on Monday.
The victim’s father, who wished to be known only as Abd Halim, 42, said his eldest daughter was only 16 when she died last year, following a four-month battle with an illness doctors were unable to diagnose.
He said the family was still coping with the loss of their eldest daughter when tragedy struck again with the death of Abdul Rafee, three.
“Just last year, we lost our eldest child. She was sick and bedridden for about four months before she passed away, but the doctors couldn’t find out what illness she was suffering from.
“We are still grieving the loss of our eldest child, and now we have lost our youngest son too,” he said when met by Bernama at his home here yesterday.
Abd Halim said he had decided to take his family to Perak during the National Day holiday as they had not gone on a holiday together for more than a year.
He said Abdul Rafee was thrilled when he found out that they were going on a holiday.
“He was such a cheerful boy. He was always making us laugh and bringing happiness to our family. We will always cherish those moments with him.
“We will also always remember how much he loved chicken rice. Usually, he would only eat rice with soup, but a few days before the incident, he asked for chicken,” he said.
Recalling the incident, Abd Halim said he first checked the condition of the Victoria Bridge before taking Abdul Rafee for a walk along the more than 125-year-old structure.
However, Abd Halim said everything happened in an instant as they tried to make way for several people taking photographs on the bridge. Abdul Rafee then stepped on a rotten piece of wood, causing his hand to slip from his father’s grasp before he fell.
Abd Halim hoped the public would not be quick to blame him and his wife, saying they had done their best to care for and ensure the safety of their children.
He also hoped the authorities would conduct regular inspections and maintenance at tourist attractions, particularly those involving old structures, to prevent similar incidents from recurring.
Abdul Rafee was laid to rest at the Kampung Baru Muslim Cemetery here at 1 am Tuesday.
On Monday, the victim was reported to have died after he was believed to have fallen about five metres from the bridge at around 6.30 pm while visiting the site with his father.
The boy was believed to have been walking while holding his father’s hand before falling through an opening in the bridge. Following the incident, the Kuala Kangsar Municipal Council (MPKK) immediately closed public access to the iron structure of the Victoria Bridge as a safety measure. — Bernama

Title: Mercy Malaysia deploys team to Nepal as 2.2 million tonnes of debris hamper aid to flood-hit communities
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Mercy Malaysia has deployed a humanitarian team to Nepal to assess urgent needs following the catastrophic flash flood that struck the Bhote Koshi river system on Aug 26, with the team set to focus on search and rescue, emergency shelter, food, clean water and sanitation as millions of tonnes of debris hamper access to affected communities.
The disaster, triggered by an ice-and-rock avalanche and glacial collapse in the Himalayan region, sent a powerful surge of water, mud and debris through the Bhote Koshi and downstream river systems, severely affecting communities and critical infrastructure in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan and other downstream districts.
Mercy Malaysia said its team will assess the situation on the ground, engage with affected communities and local partners, and identify the most urgent humanitarian needs.
A preliminary assessment by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) estimates approximately 2.2 million tonnes of debris across the analysed flood-affected areas.
At least 11 hydropower stations and one solar plant, representing approximately 431 megawatts of generating capacity, have ceased operations.
Roads and bridges have been destroyed or blocked by massive quantities of debris, making access to affected communities increasingly difficult.
Hydropower facilities, settlements and border infrastructure have also sustained extensive damage, disrupting essential services and livelihoods.
Search and rescue operations remain ongoing, particularly in remote and difficult-to-access areas.
Authorities and responders are working to clear roads, relocate communities from high-risk areas and provide emergency assistance to those affected.
Mercy Malaysia said its initial assessment will also look at healthcare, protection, and mental health and psychosocial support.
With many communities still isolated by damaged roads, bridges and extensive debris, restoring access will be critical to ensuring humanitarian assistance reaches those most in need.
Particular attention will be given to displaced families, vulnerable groups and families searching for missing loved ones.
Mercy Malaysia will work closely with local authorities, humanitarian partners and affected communities to ensure any intervention is needs-based, coordinated and responsive to the evolving situation.
Mercy Malaysia president Datuk Dr Ahmad Faizal Mohd Perdaus said the scale of the disaster was deeply concerning, particularly for communities that remained isolated and families still searching for their loved ones.
“Our immediate priority is to understand the needs on the ground and ensure that our response reaches those who need it most,” he said.
“In situations like this, timely humanitarian action can make a critical difference.”
Mercy Malaysia is committed to working alongside local authorities, partners and communities in Nepal to provide appropriate assistance and support recovery efforts as the situation develops, he said.
The organisation said the humanitarian situation remained fluid and needs may evolve as access improves and further assessments are conducted.
It will continue to monitor developments closely and determine the next phase of its response based on assessment findings and coordination with relevant authorities and humanitarian partners.
Mercy Malaysia also called for sustained collective action and solidarity to support communities affected by the floods and extreme weather conditions.
It said every contribution could help deliver life-saving assistance, restore dignity and support affected families on their path to recovery, adding that continued support remained vital as humanitarian needs evolve and recovery efforts begin.

Title: SDEB refutes viral claims of Sungai Johor Bridge closure, says safe to cross despite vessel strike
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept — The Sungai Johor Bridge here is safe for all road users, according to Senai-Desaru Expressway Berhad (SDEB).
In a statement, SDEB said it had taken immediate action by conducting inspections and assessments of the bridge’s structural condition, following the incident of a vessel that drifted close to the bridge around 2.30 pm yesterday.
“The inspection by the technical team found that the structure of bridge is in a safe condition and can be crossed as usual. The involved vessel was also moved at 3.16 pm,” according to SDEB.
SDEB said that it always prioritises safety aspects and will continue to monitor the condition of the bridge structure from time to time to ensure the safety of highway users.
“However, users are advised to always adhere to traffic regulations and follow any safety instructions issued from time to time,” the statement also said.
Earlier, several videos and pictures depicting the incident went viral on Facebook, claiming that the bridge was unsafe to cross and temporarily closed, causing concern among highway users. — Bernama

Title: BUDI95 fuel quota back to 300 litres: How will this affect motorists?
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 3 — Five months after reducing the monthly subsidised RON95 quota from 300 litres to 200 litres, the government has restored the higher limit.
The basic monthly eligibility limit under the BUDI Madani RON95 (BUDI95) programme was raised back to 300 litres effective from September 1, with 16 million users enjoying RON95 at the subsidised price of RM1.99 a litre.
According to the Finance Ministry, the restoration took into account more orderly fuel-supply management, stronger enforcement, Malaysia’s strong economic performance and the government’s financial capacity.
It also cited the needs of Malaysians who travel long distances for their daily activities and small traders who depend on vehicles to earn a living.
But with government data showing average monthly RON95 consumption is around 100 litres, what does the restored litres mean for current consumers?
What does the 300-litre quota actually mean?
The 300 litres is a monthly eligibility ceiling for subsidised RON95, it is not a monthly allocation of free petrol.
A motorist who uses 100 litres a month will still purchase only 100 litres.
The higher ceiling means eligible Budi95 users may purchase up to 300 litres of RON95 at RM1.99 a litre, subject to the programme’s eligibility requirements.
The Finance Ministry said the basic monthly BUDI Madani eligibility limit was increased automatically from 200 litres in August to 300 litres from September 1.
For example, a motorist using 250 litres a month can now have all 250 litres within the subsidised ceiling.
Who will benefit from the change?
The restoration is most relevant to motorists with higher monthly fuel consumption.
Specifically, Malaysians who need to travel long distances for daily activities and small traders who depend on vehicles to earn a living.
For motorists who use less than 200 litres a month, the immediate difference is limited because their normal consumption was already within the previous ceiling.
In Parliament, the government said average monthly RON95 consumption was around 100 litres.
It also said 90 per cent of Malaysians use no more than 200 litres a month.
This means the higher ceiling is most relevant to the smaller group of users with higher monthly fuel consumption.
Does restoring the quota mean the subsidy bill will rise sharply?
Not necessarily.
Raising the ceiling by 100 litres does not mean every BUDI95 user will consume an additional 100 litres, its actual fiscal impact depends on how much additional subsidised fuel is purchased.
The government has previously said the 200-litre limit was sufficient for 90 per cent of Budi95 users, while the cost depended on the subsidy borne by the government on each litre.
For August 27 to September 2, the Finance Ministry set unsubsidised RON95 at RM3.82 a litre, while the subsidised BUDI95 price remained at RM1.99 a litre — bearing a subsidy of RM1.83 a litre for eligible Budi95 consumers.
This means a calculation based simply on the number of users multiplied by 100 additional litres would not represent the government’s actual additional subsidy cost.
The actual cost depends on how much additional fuel is purchased and the prevailing subsidy per litre.
What does it mean for everyday consumption?
For most motorists, the change may have little immediate effect because their monthly consumption is already below 200 litres.
The difference becomes more significant for motorists who regularly exceed that level.
For example, a motorist using 250 litres a month would have 50 litres beyond a 200-litre ceiling.
Using the government’s RM1.83-per-litre subsidy figure for August 27 to September 2 as an illustration, those 50 litres represent a difference of RM91.50.
That is a calculation based on the government’s published prices, rather than an official estimate of how much an individual motorist will save.
The actual difference would change if the unsubsidised RON95 price changes.
What should motorists watch next?
The fiscal cost of subsidising RON95 will continue to depend on fuel consumption and the market cost of the fuel, while unsubsidised prices may change from week to week, meaning the subsidy borne by the government could also change.
For motorists, the immediate change is straightforward: the basic monthly Budi95 eligibility ceiling is once again 300 litres from September 1.
As for the government, the fiscal impact will depend on how much of that additional ceiling is actually used.

Title: Second suspect arrested after Sri Petaling cable‑theft chase; remanded seven days
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Police have detained another local man to assist in investigations into a cable theft case in Sri Petaling here.
Kuala Lumpur Police Chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said the 32-year-old man was believed to be the driver of a Ford Ranger which was pursued on Monday from the Awan Besar Toll Plaza heading towards Klang (West) before the chase ended at Jalan Hang Tuah 4.
“The suspect has been remanded for seven days until Sept 8 for further investigation. He has 20 previous criminal records and six drug-related records,” he said in a statement today.
On Monday, a police team fired several shots before detaining a 29-year-old man suspected of cable theft after the Ford Ranger driven by his accomplice attempted to flee a police inspection in Sri Petaling.
In the 9.30 am incident, the vehicle attempted to ram police officers before skidding and crashing into a grey Mazda at Jalan Hang Tuah 4, after which the driver fled the scene.
A search of the vehicle uncovered various tools believed to be used for cable theft, along with several suspected stolen cables.
The case is being investigated under Sections 307, 427 and 379 of the Penal Code, as well as Section 42(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987. — Bernama

Title: Sunway Lagoon says all injured guests discharged, keeps roller coaster closed pending probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — The roller coaster attraction involved in the August 22, 2026 incident at Sunway Lagoon theme park in Subang Jaya, which is believed to have stopped abruptly after failing to move forward during a ride, remains closed while investigations are ongoing.
Sunway Lagoon Sdn Bhd said in a statement today that it continues to work closely with the relevant authorities and is providing its full cooperation throughout the investigation.
“Sunway Theme Parks remains firmly committed to maintaining the highest standards of safety and to ensuring the well-being of everyone who visits our parks,” it said.
Sunway Theme Parks confirms that all guests who were admitted to the hospital for further observation following the incident have now been discharged.
“We recognise that the incident was distressing for those involved and caused understandable concern among their families.
“We sincerely regret what our guests experienced and remain in close contact with those affected to provide the necessary assistance and support,” it added.
The company emphasised that the safety and well-being of its guests is its top priority.
“We understand that the incident has also raised concerns among our guests and the wider public about the safety of our attractions, and we take these concerns seriously,” it said. — Bernama

Title: SMART prepared for Nepal deployment, with logistics and personnel on standby, says commander
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — The Special Malaysia Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (SMART) has its personnel and logistics on standby for possible deployment to Nepal.
SMART Commander Senior Fire Superintendent I (PgKB I) Abdul Manaf Che Isa said the team’s preparations encompassed the physical and mental readiness of its personnel, as well as specialised equipment, communication systems and medical requirements to support on-ground operations.
“The SMART team is ready physically and mentally, and prepared for any deployment for this mission. Logistical preparations, namely the use of specialised equipment, communications and health, are also on standby,” he said in a statement today.
He said the readiness would allow SMART to be mobilised according to the required form and scale of deployment upon receiving instructions to carry out the mission.
Additionally, he said the Nepalese government had yet to determine the number of personnel required. Therefore, SMART was prepared to be mobilised as a light, medium or skeleton team.
“This mission also depends on Nepal, whether the focus is on search and rescue (SAR) or Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) missions.
“As of today, the SAR focus (in Nepal) is prioritising tunnel rescue, which is actively being carried out by several teams from China, India and Korea,” he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim previously said SMART would assist in search and rescue (SAR) operations in Nepal following the flood disaster, including locating and bringing home affected Malaysians.
SMART would also assist the Malaysian Embassy in Nepal in coordinating aid and ensuring the safety and welfare of Malaysians affected by the disaster. — Bernama

Title: Perhilitan relocates elephant ‘Sulong Chalil’ to Terengganu Taman Negara after Gerik recapture
Article:
IPOH, Sept 2 — A wild male elephant known as “Sulong Chalil” has been relocated today to Terengganu Taman Negara through the Tasik Kenyir entrance, a natural forest habitat suitable for wild elephants.
The Department of Wildlife and National Parks (Perhilitan) of Peninsular Malaysia said that the department has carried out monitoring and rescue efforts, with the relocation aimed at providing a safer environment and reducing the risk of road accidents and conflicts with people.
Perhilitan emphasised that the welfare of Sulong, as well as the safety of the public and operational members, is always a priority, with every action taken based on an assessment of the situation on the ground to ensure that risks to all parties are minimised.
“Perhilitan expresses its appreciation to all the agencies involved and the public for the cooperation and support given,” said the statement.
The department said that since Aug 17, the Perhilitan team has been closely monitoring Sulong’s movements and physical condition, including the injury recorded on his right leg.
Perhilitan said that as an adult male elephant, Sulong’s solitary movement is a natural behaviour and not an indication that the elephant is separated from the herd or searching for its family.
The department also said that after assessing the aspects of safety, location and Sulong’s health status, the operation to recapture the animal was successfully carried out on Aug 30 along the East-West Highway (JRTB) area in Gerik.
On Sept 1, Sulong’s relocation process was carried out by Perhilitan with the support of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and the assistance of two trained elephants, Rambai and Cheri.
“Throughout the operation, Sulong always received monitoring and veterinary treatment. The injury on his right leg is now showing positive progress and follow-up treatment will continue according to the assessment of the veterinary officer,” said the statement.
Previously, several videos, allegedly recorded by members of the public using that route, went viral on social media showing the elephant, believed to be named Sulong Chalil, walking along the shoulder of the JRTB.
The elephant in question is said to have originated from Chalil, Gua Musang before being relocated to a forest area in Gerik during a Perhilitan translocation operation, but it is believed to have moved back towards its original area through that route. — Bernama

Title: Police obtain four‑day remand for boat operator in fatal Mersing collision that left two dead
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 2 — A boat operator involved in the incident where two passenger boats collided in Kuala Sungai Mersing, killing two people last Sunday, has been remanded for four days starting today.
Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said the 33-year-old local man was arrested by a Criminal Investigation Division team of the Mersing district police headquarters (IPD) at about 12 noon yesterday to assist in the investigation.
He said the suspect was then taken to the Kota Tinggi Magistrate’s Court for a remand application under Section 117 of the Criminal Procedure Code.
“The court granted a four-day remand from Sept 2 to 5 to assist in further investigations,” he said in a statement today.
Ab Rahaman said a check found that the suspect had a criminal record related to narcotics offences, but an initial urine test on him was negative for drugs.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 304A of the Penal Code for causing death by negligence and Section 280 of the same code for operating a boat in a rash manner.
Section 304A provides for a prison sentence of up to two years or a fine or both, while Section 280 provides for a prison sentence of up to six months or a maximum fine of RM2,000 or both, if convicted.
“The investigation is in line with the investigation into the sudden death (SDR) case,” he said.
He also advised the public not to speculate or spread unverified information regarding the incident and to give the authorities time to conduct a thorough investigation.
In the incident, two individuals died while four others were injured after two boats collided.
The Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) received an emergency call regarding the incident at 9.04 pm before nine personnel from the Mersing Fire and Rescue Station were rushed to the Mersing Jetty.
The seven injured were taken to several hospitals for treatment. — Bernama

Title: Former Tabung Haji COO to be charged in Shah Alam Sessions Court tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — A former Lembaga Tabung Haji chief operating officer is expected to be charged at the Shah Alam Sessions Court tomorrow.
The Star
reported that a court e‑filing entry lists Datuk Adi Azuan Abdul Ghani as scheduled to appear before Sessions Court judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud at 9am on September 3.
The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji previously identified Adi Azuan among five senior officers subjected to disciplinary proceedings, noting that an initial proposal to dismiss four of them was later revised to demotions.
The Malaysian Anti‑Corruption Commission (MACC) has opened 14 investigation papers following the RCI’s findings on mismanagement at the agency.
MACC said it has arrested 17 individuals to date, with 10 suspects remanded as part of the ongoing probe.
The arrests include a former Tabung Haji investment director, the director of Putrajaya Perdana, the former director of Putra Perdana Construction, the former Tabung Haji chairman, the chief executive officer of Alam Maritim and a former federal minister.

Title: Minister: National Scam Response Centre returned RM5.16m to victims, from funds seized between January and July 2026
Article:
BANGI, Sept 2 — A total of RM5.16 million in scam proceeds was returned to victims between January and July 2026, representing 65 per cent of the RM7.94 million seized through the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC), said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
“For us, the return of money to victims is among the enforcement outcomes that can be directly felt by the people,” he said at a press conference after officiating the 6th International Cyber Resilience Conference (CRC) here today.
He said the figures also indicated that cyber threats were becoming increasingly serious, with the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) reporting that scam operations in Southeast Asia alone generated tens of billions of dollars annually.
Touching on figures for online sexual abuse, he said cases involving child sexual abuse material (CSAM) increased from 68 in 2024 to 152 last year, while another 100 cases were recorded up to the middle of this year.
“As of April 2026, through Ops Cyber Guardian, involving the cooperation of seven countries, we have successfully led to the arrest of 69 individuals and seized 498,694 digital files, including 205,000 files of child sexual abuse material,” he said.
In addition, he revealed that as of Aug 28, a total of 746 Malaysians had fallen victim to fake job offers abroad.
Therefore, he said, the government and enforcement agencies needed to leverage artificial intelligence (AI) applications to tackle increasingly sophisticated cybercriminals, while taking into account the cross-border nature of such crimes.
He said cybercriminals today were no longer conventional criminals, but operated in syndicates and leveraged rapidly evolving technologies.
“In the context of our discussion, it is about how these AI tools can be utilised among policymakers and enforcement agencies to face criminals who are also sophisticated.
“They (criminals) also use cyber technology and are far ahead of us. They operate across borders and are not conventional criminals, but crime syndicates.
“Generative AI is a new phenomenon. When criminal perpetrators have already mastered it, we cannot remain stuck in our old ways,” he said.
Themed Navigating Challenges and Opportunities in Global Cyber Resilience, CRC 2026 emphasises the nation’s capability to not only prevent cyber threats but also prepare, respond, recover and adapt when disruptions occur, while ensuring the nation’s critical functions continue to operate.
CRC 2026 is taking place over three days in a hybrid format, with around 321 physical attendees and 149 online attendees from within the country and abroad.
Among the strategic focuses of the conference are two forums related to the Cyber Crime Fusion Centre (CCFC), in line with the CCFC Establishment Study, which is now entering its second phase, encompassing the development of a Governance Model and an Operational Model.
The study involves the Home Affairs Ministry (KDN) through the Institute of Public Security of Malaysia (IPSOM), in collaboration with the Cyber Security Academia Malaysia (CSAM) and relevant strategic partners. — Bernama

Title: Felda pledges full cooperation as MACC opens six probes into agency, FIC
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — The Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) will extend its full cooperation to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) in its investigation involving the agency and its subsidiary companies.
In a statement today, Felda said it fully respected the ongoing investigation process to ensure that it was carried out transparently, fairly and comprehensively.
“Felda does not compromise on any form of corruption, misappropriation, abuse of power or violation of the law that could undermine the interests of settlers and the institution,” it said.
Felda also called on all parties to respect the investigation process.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said today that the commission had opened six new investigation papers into allegations of misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving Felda and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC).
Abd Halim said the investigations followed information received on Aug 24 concerning projects and investments undertaken by the management of Felda and FIC between 2010 and 2020. — Bernama

Title: Anwar warns US-Iran hostilities risk wider regional conflict, urges return to diplomacy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today urged the United States (US) and Iran to immediately halt further escalation and return to diplomacy amid renewed hostilities between the two countries.
He warned that the latest exchange of strikes, which has extended beyond the immediate parties and into other states in the region, risks drawing the wider Middle East into an even more destructive conflict.
In a Facebook post, Anwar said the party with the greatest capacity to shape events bears a particular responsibility to exercise restraint and prevent further escalation.
“The sovereignty of other states cannot be cast aside. No military objective justifies exposing civilians to an expanding conflict,” he said.
Anwar also cautioned against economic measures that inflict hardship on civilians and impede diplomatic engagement, saying such actions risk exacerbating rather than resolving the crisis.
“I urge the United States and Iran to halt further escalation and return immediately to diplomacy and the understandings reached in June,” he said.
The Prime Minister stressed that the conflict could ultimately be resolved only through political and diplomatic means, adding that the world must not be made to pay the price for a wider regional war.  — Bernama

Title: Claim on Malaysia recruiting 200,000 Bangladeshi workers not Bangladesh’s official position, says Fahmi
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — A statement by a Bangladeshi junior minister claiming that Malaysia planned to recruit 200,000 workers from the country does not represent the official position of the Bangladeshi government, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R Ramanan had confirmed that a junior member had made the statement on behalf of the Bangladesh government and that it did not represent the country’s official position.
“I contacted the Human Resources Minister regarding the matter and he informed me that it was not an official statement from the Bangladesh government.
“It was issued by, as I understand, a junior minister. Therefore, it does not represent an official decision of the Bangladesh government,” he told a press conference after the Cabinet meeting here today.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said the Cabinet had been informed that 1,476 Myanmar nationals held at immigration detention depots would be repatriated to their home country at the end of this month.
He said all of them had signed documents indicating their agreement to return to Myanmar voluntarily.
“Of the more than 10,000 Myanmar nationals detained at immigration depots, 5,000 names were screened by the Home Ministry and subsequently submitted to the Myanmar Embassy.
“From that list, Myanmar has agreed to receive 1,476 of them, and the repatriation will take place at the end of September,” he said.
Fahmi also said the Foreign Ministry had received assurances from the Myanmar government that the safety of those being repatriated would be guaranteed.
“Wisma Putra and, in particular, the Foreign Minister have informed us that nothing will happen to them. What has been agreed and understood with the Myanmar authorities is that the 1,476 out of the 5,000 who have been approved for return will be safe in Myanmar,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain to hit KL and 12 states until 7pm, says MetMalaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur and 12 states until 7pm tonight.
MetMalaysia in a statement today announced that the bad weather is expected to occur throughout Perlis, Kedah, Terengganu as well as three areas in Penang including Seberang Perai Utara, Seberang Perai Tengah dan Seberang Perai Selatan.
In Perak, the affected areas are Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang, Muallim, Selama, Kerian and Larut Matang, Kelantan (Gua Musang, Jeli, Tanah Merah, Kuala Krai, Machang, Pasir Puteh and Bachok) and Pahang (Rompin, Pekan, Cameron Highlands, Lipis, Raub, Temerloh, Bentong, Bera and Jerantut).
Similar warnings have also been issued for Selangor (Hulu Selangor, Gombak and Hulu Langat), Negeri Sembilan (Tampin, Rembau, Jelebu, Seremban, Jempol and Kuala Pilah), and Johor (Segamat).
In Sarawak, severe weather is expected in Sarikei (Sarikei, Maradong and Julau), Kapit (Song) while in Sabah, it will affect the West Coast (Ranau), Sandakan (Paitan, Telupid and Labuk & Sugut). — Bernama

Title: Fahmi: Sarawak’s Malaysia Day celebration to be held indoors at BCCK; outdoor events off due to haze
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — Malaysia Day 2026 celebrations on September 16 will be held as scheduled at the Borneo Convention Centre Kuching (BCCK), Sarawak, but outdoor events cannot be held due to the worrying haze situation in Kuching and Serian.
Communications Minister and chairman of the 2026 National Day and Malaysia Day Celebrations (HKHM) Main Committee Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the decision was made after taking into account the haze situation in both areas.
“The Cabinet also took note that the rather worrying haze situation in Kuching and Serian means that outdoor events cannot proceed.
“But the Malaysia Day celebrations will be held indoors on the evening of September 16,” he told a post-Cabinet meeting press conference here today.
Fahmi also said the Cabinet was informed by the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry today that the cloud-seeding operation in Sarawak could not proceed as the cloud formations currently detected were unsuitable, due to wind movements that could potentially carry the clouds towards the South China Sea.
“So, if cloud seeding were carried out, the rain would not fall in the areas where it is needed,” he said.
Three areas in Sarawak recorded hazardous Air Pollutant Index readings as of 8 am today, with the Serian District Police Headquarters recording the highest reading at 320, followed by Kuching (318) and Samarahan (302).
Meanwhile, Fahmi said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim expressed his appreciation and congratulations to the entire team that successfully organised the 2026 National Day celebrations at Dataran Putrajaya on Monday.
He said more than 100,000 people attended the celebrations, while more than 10,000 people participated as contingents and in the human graphic formation performance.
“We believe the programmes held alongside the main celebrations also provided visitors to Putrajaya with a new and positive experience in conjunction with National Day,” he said. — Bernama

Title: MACC ready to probe N. Sembilan Pakatan allocation if misuse proven, says commissioner
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is ready to investigate if there is evidence of misuse involving the RM180,000 allocation granted to each Pakatan Harapan (PH) state assemblyman prior to the dissolution of the Negeri Sembilan State Assembly on June 5.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said reports accompanied by evidence showing fund misuse or legal offences would serve as a basis for the commission to initiate an investigation.
However, he noted that MACC currently saw no issue regarding the approval of the allocations, as a legitimate government had the right to introduce policies or approve funds provided they did not contradict the law or the Federal Constitution.
“If it is a legitimate government, there is no issue for them to introduce a policy or make an allocation, provided it does not contradict the law and the Federal Constitution,” he told a press conference at the MACC Headquarters here today.
Abd Halim added that the situation differed for a caretaker government, which should not introduce new policies that could bind an incoming administration post-election.
On Aug 26, 17 former PH state assemblymen and two assembly coordinators from the previous Negeri Sembilan administration were directed to return their August and September allocations following the dissolution of the state assembly on June 5.
Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said the allocations were approved on June 3 and credited into the recipients’ accounts on June 4, a day before the assembly was dissolved.
He said the decision to demand the return of the funds was made to ensure state government funds complied with recipient status following dissolution, as well as to maintain financial transparency and integrity.
The Menteri Besar’s Office will issue demand letters for repayment, giving recipients 30 days to return the funds.
Meanwhile, in a separate case, Abd Halim said the MACC had yet to receive a letter regarding a corruption case involving former human resources minister Datuk Seri M. Saravanan.
“Regarding the letter, we have not received it from the stated party. We are still waiting,” he said.
Commenting on allegations that a key witness in the case had died, Abd Halim said details regarding the matter fell under a confidential investigation process.
“Details regarding the process and allegations that a key witness has died pertain to confidential investigation procedures known only to the investigating officers and top MACC management.
“Therefore, whether the case remains strong and why it is being pursued is a legal matter,” he said.
On Aug 28, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim called on all parties to allow the legal process to run its course in Saravanan’s case, noting that the matter fell under the jurisdiction of MACC and the Attorney-General’s Chambers.
Saravanan previously said his letter to the Prime Minister was not meant to seek intervention or drop the charges, but to explain his position on the matter.
Earlier, the Tapah MP pleaded not guilty at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court to three corruption charges amounting to RM1.097 million related to the approval of foreign worker quotas. — Bernama

Title: Serian and Kuching record hazardous API levels in Sarawak at 4pm; more areas very unhealthy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Two areas in Sarawak recorded hazardous Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4 pm today, with the Serian district police headquarters recording the highest reading at 325.
According to the Malaysian API Management System (APIMS), Kuching recorded a hazardous API reading of 309.
Meanwhile, five areas in Sarawak recorded very unhealthy API readings: Samarahan (287), Sarikei (256), Sibu (248), Sri Aman (247) and Mukah (205).
Meanwhile, 16 stations recorded API readings at the unhealthy level, with Bintulu in Sarawak recording the highest reading at 192, followed by Kapit (190), Politeknik Kota Kinabalu in Sabah (178), Keningau (175) and Kota Kinabalu (173).
Other areas recording unhealthy API readings were Labuan (173), Samalaju in Sarawak (172), Kimanis in Sabah (171), ILP Miri, Sarawak (170), Limbang, Sarawak (169), Miri, Sarawak (166), Johan Setia in Selangor (159), Putrajaya (151), Nilai in Negeri Sembilan (151), Sandakan in Sabah (136) and Seremban in Negeri Sembilan (109).
Forty-five stations recorded API readings at the moderate level, while none recorded readings in the good category.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality; 51 to 100, moderate; 101 to 200, unhealthy; 201 to 300, very unhealthy; and readings above 300 are classified as hazardous. — Bernama

Title: MACC: Six Felda and FIC cases under investigation, arrests imminent
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has opened six new investigation papers into alleged misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption involving the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) and its subsidiary, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC), with several arrests expected beginning next week.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the investigations followed information received on Aug 24 regarding the implementation of projects and investments by Felda and FIC management between 2010 and 2020.
“We received the information on Aug 24 and, through Ops Fella, the six investigation papers opened involve issues concerning the purchase and investment in assets by Felda and FIC, which are suspected of involving elements of misappropriation, abuse of power and corruption,” he told a press conference at the MACC headquarters here today.
The six matters are the purchase of Tataran Aras Sdn Bhd in Limbang, Sarawak; the acquisition of Grand Borneo Hotel Sdn Bhd in Sabah; the purchase of Grand Plaza Serviced Apartments in London; the establishment of Felda Wellness Corporation Sdn Bhd; the acquisition of Felda House and Grand Felda House; and alleged misappropriation in the development of the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project.
“MACC is also reviewing an old investigation paper involving the Park City Grand Plaza property, which has yet to be closed and is currently undergoing a mutual legal assistance (MLA) process,” he said.
So far, 12 individuals have had their statements recorded, comprising three FIC board members, an FIC secretary, two FIC Legal Division officers, a valuer, three individuals from law firms, a Kuala Lumpur Land and Mines Office (PTG) officer and an officer from the Kuala Lumpur Valuation and Property Services Department.
Abd Halim said several arrests were expected to be made in stages beginning early next week, while the amount of corruption proceeds believed to be involved had yet to be determined as the investigation was still at an early stage.
He said MACC also received information on Aug 24 from the chairman of the Pertubuhan Badan Bertindak Generasi Palong (Perbagi) regarding concerns over the quality of oil palm seedlings and the implementation of oil palm development and replanting programmes at Felda Palong 7.
He said the information concerned a development programme reportedly benefiting about 450 settlers, including issues related to supply and delivery.
“MACC gives an assurance that its investigation into Felda’s management will be conducted comprehensively, fairly and professionally, based on the principle of the rule of law,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Perak police launch investigations over toddler’s fatal fall at Victoria Bridge
Article:
IPOH, Sept  2 — Police have opened two investigation papers into the death of a three-year-old boy who is believed to have fallen about five metres from Victoria Bridge in Enggor, near Kuala Kangsar, yesterday.
Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the investigation papers were opened under Section 31(1) of the Child Act 2001, with several individuals summoned to assist the investigation.
Based on statements from several witnesses, the victim is believed to have fallen while walking after stepping into a gap in the bridge’s structure.
“Preliminary investigations found no element of negligence in the incident. We are awaiting the post-mortem results from Kuala Kangsar Hospital,” he told a press conference at the Sungai Siput District Police Headquarters (IPD) here today.
Meanwhile, State Housing and Local Government Committee chairperson Sandrea Ng Shy Ching said the Kuala Kangsar Municipal Council (MPKK) had immediately closed visitor access to the steel structure section of the bridge as a safety measure.
She said the closure would remain in place temporarily pending the replacement of worn and rotten track timbers, installation of additional safety measures and confirmation that the area is safe to reopen.
“According to MPKK, the bridge has been monitored periodically, with the latest physical inspection conducted on June 30, 2026.
“Prior to this incident, an application for funds had already been submitted for maintenance work, including the replacement of about 60 worn-out track timbers,” she said in a statement.
Sandrea added that MPKK was also seeking about RM50,000 as an immediate allocation to install safety netting beneath the bridge while awaiting funds for other repair works.
She said the overall safety of the site would also be reviewed in consultation with the relevant parties to determine appropriate improvement measures.
The victim, Abdul Rafee Abdul Halim, reportedly fell through a gap in the bridge at about 6.30 pm yesterday while walking with his father and died in the incident.
The more than 125-year-old Victoria Bridge is a historic railway bridge in Enggor. — Bernama

Title: MACC investigator: Muhyiddin abused powers as PM to help Jana Wibawa contractors
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 2 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin abused his powers as a prime minister when he acted to help Bumiputera contractors to eventually get government projects under the Jana Wibawa programme, an anti-corruption investigator told the High Court.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) senior assistant commissioner Mazery Mohd Zaini, who was the investigating officer for Muhyiddin’s case, said this while testifying as the 29th prosecution witness in the latter’s power abuse trial.
Mazery said he had also previously investigated Bumiputera Contractors Association of Malaysia (PKBM) president and KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd managing director Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff as a suspect in a corruption case.
Mazery confirmed that Azman was not remanded or charged in that case.
Mazery explained that this was because investigations showed that the businessman had given money to Muhyiddin’s Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia after being asked to do so by the then Prime Minister.
“Yes, I investigated this complaint which stated that Datuk Azman Yusoff had asked for and received bribes from companies as a reward for helping those companies receive Jana Wibawa projects,” he told lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin.
“Based on the investigations, it was found there was abuse of power by the prime minister at that time, where he had helped by instructing the finance minister to handle applications by companies,” he said, adding that Azman was then made into a witness instead.
When asked by Wan Shaharuddin to explain why he said Muhyiddin had abused his powers as prime minister, Mazery said this was due to Muhyiddin’s actions in relation to companies who were applying for Jana Wibawa projects.
“Because of his action at that time, instructing the finance minister to help companies who applied and subsequently the companies which were successfully helped made donations. Companies which successfully obtained projects had donated to the party Bersatu,” Mazery said.
Muhyiddin was prime minister from March 1, 2020 until Aug 20, 2021.
Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Hisyam Teh Poh Teik immediately objected to Mazery’s testimony that claimed his client had abused his powers as prime minister, saying that this should be left to the High Court to conclude.
While Hisyam asked for this part of Mazery’s testimony to be expunged or removed from court records, High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin said it does not have to be expunged as it involved the investigator’s investigations.
Recording Hisyam’s objections, the judge said she will make her own conclusions: “But it’s not binding on the court, I have to make my own finding.”
Golf allowed during Covid-19 lockdown in Malaysia
Previously, Azman as the 27th prosecution witness said he had in July 2020 joined the Tan Sri Muhyiddin Charity Golf (TSMCG) golf tournament at Tropicana Golf Club in the morning, before attending a one-on-one meeting with Muhyiddin at 3pm at the club on the same day.
Azman said Muhyiddin had in the meeting spontaneously told him that contractors could donate directly to Bersatu, and that Muhyiddin had also told him about the Jana Wibawa programme then.
Muhyiddin’s lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad had previously challenged Azman’s testimony about the July 2020 golfing event by saying that the TSMCG tournament only took place in October 2020.
Yesterday, Tropicana Golf Club’s security chief Saravanan Subaramaniam told the High Court that the club’s computer system showed that Muhyiddin and 14 other players including an “Azman” had played a golf game there on July 19, 2020.
Today, Mazery said he was informed on July 23, 2026 by his fellow MACC investigator about the exact date of this golf game, namely July 19, 2020.
Mazery told Wan Shaharuddin that he had not received any notice of alibi from Muhyiddin’s lawyers to show where their client was on July 19, 2020.
Mazery confirmed that he had seen Muhyiddin’s May 1, 2020 speech, where the Malaysian government had allowed golf to be played amid the Conditional Movement Control Order (CMCO) during the Covid-19 pandemic.
Mazery read out an excerpt of that speech, where Malaysians were told that outdoor sports such as jogging, cycling, playing golf and running in small groups not exceeding 10 persons were allowed, with the condition that they practise social distancing.
Previously, Muhyiddin’s lawyer Amer had also challenged Azman by saying that sports were not allowed during the Movement Control Order (MCO) in May 2020, but Azman said playing golf while maintaining social distancing was already allowed in May 2020.
In this trial, Muhyiddin is facing seven charges, namely four counts of alleged power abuse to obtain RM225.3 million in bribes for his party, Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia (from Nepturis Sdn Bhd, Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff, KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd, Bukhary Equity Sdn Bhd and Mamfor Sdn Bhd), and three counts of alleged money laundering involving money that Bersatu received from Bukhary Equity.
The trial is scheduled to resume tomorrow, with Azman expected to be further cross-examined by Muhyiddin’s lawyers.

Title: Don’t sacrifice independent oversight for speed in Sabah’s water crisis fixes, says former Water Dept director
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 2 — Sabah’s recurring water supply problems require urgent and practical solutions, but the push for faster action should not come at the expense of independent engineering judgement, said Datuk Amarjit Singh.
The former Sabah Water Department director said a clear distinction must be maintained between an engineering consultancy practice and a commercial service provider, particularly when companies supplying water infrastructure, equipment, or specialised technologies are also proposing solutions.
“The issue is not whether service providers have the technical capability to contribute. Many possess valuable operational experience, specialised technology, and the ability to deliver projects quickly. The issue is independence,” he said in a statement.
Amarjit said companies recommending technologies in which they have a commercial interest could face an inherent potential conflict, making independent assessment important.
He pointed out that under Malaysia’s engineering regulatory framework, an Engineering Consultancy Practice registered with the Board of Engineers Malaysia (BEM) has a professional role in providing independent engineering advice, including feasibility assessments, design, and certification within its lawful scope.
“Employing a professional engineer does not by itself make a product manufacturer, operator, or service company an independent engineering consultancy practice,” he said.
Major water supply decisions, including desalination, water reuse, additional storage, leakage reduction, and watershed protection, should begin with an impartial assessment of available options, he said.
Amarjit said companies recommending technologies in which they have a commercial interest could face an inherent potential conflict, making independent assessment important. — The Borneo Post pic
For advanced technologies such as desalination, feasibility studies should consider not only capital costs but also energy consumption, reliability, environmental impacts, waste management, maintenance, replacement costs, and whole-of-life expenditure.
“Consultants should provide independent professional advice and evaluate the available options; service providers should bring proven technologies, specialist knowledge, implementation capability and operational support,” he said.
Amarjit stressed he is not arguing against service providers, but calling for their expertise to complement independent engineering advice.
“The party selling or operating a solution should not be the sole party deciding that the same solution is the best one for the public,” he said.
He called for major water projects to undergo independent engineering assessment before commitments are made, saying this would strengthen procurement decisions and ensure Sabah’s resources are directed towards solutions that are technically sound, environmentally responsible, and financially sustainable.
“Sabah’s water future deserves decisions based on evidence rather than on the attractiveness of a packaged solution. Speed is important but so are transparency, accountability, and professional independence,” he said.
Amarjit added that his comments were intended to contribute to public discussion on infrastructure governance and water security and were not directed at or intended to allege wrongdoing by any particular company or organisation. — The Borneo Post

Title: Batik Air agrees to resume Miri-KL flights after deputy minister’s request
Article:
MIRI, Sept 2 — Batik Air has agreed to resume its Miri-Kuala Lumpur services following a formal request by Deputy Minister of Tourism, Arts and Culture Chiew Choon Man.
The Miri MP said the commencement date, flight frequency and schedule would be announced by the airline in due course.
Chiew said he had received increasing feedback from Miri residents over the difficulty of securing flights between Miri and Kuala Lumpur, particularly during weekends, public holidays and peak travel periods.
“Flights are often heavily booked, and airfares can become very expensive when seat availability is limited,” he said in a statement yesterday.
He said he had formally written to Batik Air’s chief executive officer Datuk Chandran Rama Muthy, urging the airline to review the commercial viability of the Miri-Kuala Lumpur sector and consider returning to Miri.
Chiew said current market conditions should be reassessed, noting that while the airline’s previous operations had been affected by challenges such as volatility in fuel and aviation costs, demand for travel between Miri and Kuala Lumpur remained strong.
He also stressed that Miri’s potential should not be assessed based solely on the city’s population, as it serves a wider catchment area encompassing northern Sarawak and neighbouring Brunei Darussalam.
“With suitable flight timings and competitive fares, there is further potential to attract Bruneian passengers who use Miri as an alternative gateway to Kuala Lumpur and onward destinations,” he said.
Chiew welcomed Batik Air’s positive response, describing the return of another airline operator as important for Miri.
He said additional capacity would give passengers more choices, improve connectivity and help ease pressure on seat availability during periods of strong demand.
“Greater competition and additional capacity can also contribute towards a healthier and more competitive airfare environment for travellers.
“Improved air connectivity is also important for Miri’s wider economic and tourism development,” he said.
Chiew said in his capacity as Miri MP and deputy minister, he would continue working with airlines and relevant stakeholders to strengthen Miri’s connectivity.
He added that his office was prepared to support Batik Air in developing the route, including facilitating engagement with tourism industry players, travel agents, business associations and other relevant stakeholders in Miri and Brunei.
He also thanked Batik Air Malaysia’s management for listening to the concerns and needs of Miri residents and responding positively to the request. — The Borneo Post

Title: US embassy shifts Sabah travel status to ‘relaxed’ after security improvements
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Sept 2 — The United States is encouraging its citizens and international travellers to visit Sabah, citing significant improvements in security and a corresponding relaxation of travel advisories, said US Embassy Kuala Lumpur Chargé d'Affaires David Gamble.
He noted that the US lowered its travel advisory for Sabah and Borneo earlier this year, a move that has prompted several other nations to review their own warnings.
“Now it is at a very relaxed travel status. Many countries are following America’s lead and reviewing their travel advisories as well,” Gamble said during the launch of the Freedom 250 Sabah programme at the Tanjung Aru State Library today.
“This reflects the improved security and how safe it is to visit Sabah. We want to encourage more tourists to visit Sabah because Sabah is a wonderful place to visit.”
The shift follows a period of heightened caution that began in July 2014 after a series of kidnapping-for-ransom incidents along the east coast.
In February, the US Embassy downgraded its advisory for Eastern Sabah to Level 1, advising citizens to exercise only normal precautions, though maritime areas and offshore islands remain at Level 2. Japan has similarly lowered its advisory for coastal areas from Kudat to Tawau to Level 1.
When asked about the possibility of establishing a US consulate in Kota Kinabalu, Gamble clarified that there are no plans to do so in the coming years.
The diplomatic push coincides with "Freedom 250," a three-day series of events in Kota Kinabalu commemorating the 250th anniversary of American independence. The programme celebrates the longstanding ties between the US and Sabah through education, culture, sports, and people-to-people exchanges.
Highlights of the celebration include the travelling Freedom 250 Exhibition at the Tanjung Aru State Library, STEM workshops supported by McDermott and ConocoPhillips, and the English Access Scholarship Programme. In the sporting arena, three-time Olympic gold medallist Shannon Boxx is leading a football clinic for up to 500 young Sabahan athletes.
The festivities will culminate tomorrow with the Great American Sabah State Fair and Freedom 250 Fun Run at Padang Merdeka from 3pm to 10pm. The fair will feature American-inspired cuisine, local vendors, and a live performance by the US Pacific Band. Additionally, American cinematic classics such as “Back to the Future” and “The Incredibles” will be screened at City Cineplex, City Mall.
These celebrations run parallel to the 22nd Pacific Partnership mission in Sabah, where approximately 400 US service members and personnel from eight partner nations, including the UK, Japan, and Australia, are collaborating with local communities on engineering projects, medical outreach, and disaster preparedness.
Gamble noted that these diverse programmes reflect the breadth of the US-Sabah relationship, providing young Sabahans with direct access to American innovation, education, and culture.

Title: Retiree loses RM1.417m after transferring savings across multiple accounts in phone‑call scam
Article:
KUANTAN, Sept 2 — A retiree of a national multinational oil and gas company suffered a loss of RM1.417 million after being duped by a telephone fraud syndicate between May and yesterday.
Pahang acting police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the victim, a 66-year-old man, received a call from an unknown individual on May 19 who claimed that the victim was involved in money laundering activities.
He said the victim was then instructed to open an Agrobank account and transfer his savings to the account for the purpose of checking by the authorities.
“After opening the account, a man came to meet the victim in his residential area and the victim handed over his bank card and PIN number to the man,” he said in a statement.
Meanwhile, he said the victim had also transferred money from his Employees Provident Fund (EPF), Amanah Saham Berhad and Tabung Haji accounts as well as pawn gold proceeds totalling RM1,417,210 to the Agrobank account as of yesterday.
Azry Akmar said the victim then realised that the money in the account had been transferred to six different accounts and withdrawn via an automated teller machine (ATM) without his knowledge.
He advised the public to seek advice from the nearest police station before taking any action after receiving a suspicious call to avoid becoming a victim of fraud.
“The public is also advised to check the account number via the Semak Mule website before making any transaction and to contact the National Scam Response Centre (NSRC) at 997 if they are a victim of fraud,” he said, adding that the case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code. — Bernama

Title: One teen found dead as search continues for three others missing in Tanjung Balau
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 2 — The body of one of four teenagers feared drowned at Tanjung Lompat Beach in Tanjung Balau was recovered this afternoon.
The victim, identified as Alif Taqiudin Kamal Hasrul Mohamad, was found by the search and rescue (SAR) team and members of the public at 1.25pm, approximately 800 metres from the location where he was last seen.
Kota Tinggi police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohd Syamsuri Mohamad confirmed that the body was identified by family members and has since been transported to Kota Tinggi Hospital.
“The SAR operation for the other three victims is still ongoing,” he told reporters today.
The tragedy unfolded at 7.45am this morning when a group of 15 teenagers, camping in conjunction with the school holidays, encountered distress in the water.
While six of them drowned, two 16-year-old students — identified as Mohamad Faqrul Islander Abdullah and Muhammad Afiq Ruzaini Mazlan — were successfully rescued. Four others remain missing.
Fire and Rescue Department operations commander Soleh Nasir noted that the rescue efforts have been severely hampered by strong undersea currents, rough beach conditions, and high winds.
“We are using the surface searching technique in this SAR operation,” he stated.
A massive coordination effort is currently underway, involving 30 personnel from the police, the Fire and Rescue Department, marine police, and the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA). They are being supported by the Tanjung Balau Fishermen's Association and local sailors.

Title: Johor dengue cases jump 131pc to 9,954 as infections rise across districts
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Sept 2 — Johor recorded 9,954 dengue cases as of Epid Week (ME) 34 this year, an increase of 131.3 per cent compared to 4,304 cases for the same period last year.
State Health and Environment Committee Chairman Ling Tian Soon said of the total, 4,520 cases or 45.4 per cent were reported from outbreak localities while 5,434 cases or 54.6 per cent were from non-outbreak localities.
He said for ME34 alone, a total of 664 dengue fever cases were reported, an increase of two per cent compared to 651 cases in the previous week.
“Of the total dengue cases reported throughout ME34, 308 cases or 46.4 per cent were reported from outbreak localities and 356 cases or 53.6 per cent from non-outbreak localities,” he said in a statement today.
Ling said Johor Bahru recorded the highest number of cases in the week in question with 495 cases or 74.6 per cent of the total cases, followed by Kulai (120), Batu Pahat (19), Segamat (nine), Kota Tinggi (seven), Muar and Pontian with four cases each.
Meanwhile, a total of 13 deaths due to dengue were recorded up to ME33 this year compared to eight deaths for the same period in 2025, an increase of 62.5 per cent.
He said a total of 3,745 compounds with a total value of RM1.87 million were issued through enforcement activities throughout the year with 80.2 per cent of them paid. — Bernama

Title: MMEA detains tugboat and dredger over suspected ship‑to‑ship transfer; RM260m oil cargo seized off Tanjung Buai
Article:
KOTA TINGGI, Sept 2 — The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) detained two vessels suspected of carrying out unauthorised ship-to-ship activities in national waters early yesterday morning, with the value of the seized goods estimated at RM260 million.
Tanjung Sedili Zone Maritime acting director Maritime Commander Mohd Najib Sam said the action was carried out at 3.20am after receiving public information regarding two suspicious vessels seen huddled together at a position about 1.4 nautical miles northwest of Tanjung Buai.
“Further inspection also found a quantity of oil cargo believed to have no documents relating to ownership and delivery.
The two vessels, consisting of a tugboat and a dredger, each registered in Malaysia, along with the oil cargo, have been detained for further investigation,” he said.
Mohd Najib said the tugboat was operated by a crew of five including the skipper, consisting of local and Indonesian citizens aged between 26 and 58 years, while the dredger was operated by a crew of 13 including the skipper, all local citizens aged between 22 and 51 years.
The case is being investigated under Section 491B(1)(K) of the Merchant Shipping Ordinance (OPS) 1952 for suspected ship-to-ship activities without the permission of the Malaysian Director of Marine.
The case is also being investigated under Section 491B(1)(L) of the OPS 1952 for anchoring without permission and the Customs Act 1967 regarding the discovery of a cargo of oil suspected of not having the relevant documents. — Bernama
